# Velvet UI

> Glassy SwiftUI components with spring motion and haptics for iOS 18+ and macOS 15+. Frosted glass over solid neutral page tones, no borders, VoiceOver and Reduce Motion built in. MIT.

Add it with Swift Package Manager (https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git, product `VelvetUI`, from 0.2.0) and `import VelvetUI`, or copy a single component and the core it needs into your app with the CLI: download https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui/main/scripts/velvet.swift, then run `swift velvet.swift add <Name>`. Inject a `DSTheme` once at the root with `.dsTheme(DSTheme(style: .sunset))`, wrap screens in `DSScreen(backdrop: true)` for the glass look, use design tokens only (never raw colors, fonts or spacing), and read AGENTS.md first.

---
<!-- source: AGENTS.md -->

# Velvet UI: guide for AI coding agents

This file is for agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Xcode) writing SwiftUI that **uses** Velvet UI, and for the people reviewing their output. It covers the rules, the token cheat sheet, copyable patterns and the mistakes to avoid.

- Everything an agent needs in one file: [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt). Index: [`llms.txt`](llms.txt).
- Every component as data (source files, dependencies, docs): [`registry.json`](registry.json).
- Contributing to Velvet UI itself? Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [docs/engineering-notes.md](docs/engineering-notes.md) too.

**Use it in your app's agent setup.** Add one line to your project's `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.cursor/rules`:

```text
UI uses Velvet UI. Follow https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui/main/AGENTS.md
```

## Setup (once per app)

Pick one of the two install paths and don't mix them in one target: the package and copied sources define the same types.

**Swift Package (recommended).** `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`, product `VelvetUI`, from `0.2.0`. Then `import VelvetUI` in every file with UI.

**Copy the source.** Velvet ships a small CLI that copies one component, plus the shared core it needs, into your app:

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui/main/scripts/velvet.swift
swift velvet.swift add DSTabBar --dest MyApp/VelvetUI   # also: list, info <name>
```

Copied files compile in Swift 5 and Swift 6 language mode and need no `import`. Previews aren't copied. Running `add` again updates untouched files and never overwrites your edits without `--force`.

**Theme at the root.** Both paths need exactly one theme injected at the top of the view tree:

```swift
import VelvetUI

@main struct MyApp: App {
    @State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)   // .sunset, .aurora, .lagoon
    var body: some Scene { WindowGroup { RootView().dsTheme(theme) } }
}
```

Velvet targets iOS 18+ and macOS 15+.

## The rules

1. **Inject one `DSTheme` with `.dsTheme(_:)` at the root.** Without it every view silently uses a shared default, and changing "your" theme does nothing.
2. **Put screens on the backdrop.** Write `DSScreen(backdrop: true) { … }` (it scrolls) or add `.dsBackdrop()` to a container. Glass needs a page tone behind it to read as glass; each style draws a flat neutral background, never a gradient.
3. **Reach for a component before building one.** See [the component chooser](#component-chooser). Velvet components already handle press feel, haptics, VoiceOver and Reduce Motion.
4. **Tokens only.** Use `DSSpacing` for padding and gaps, `DSRadius` for corners, `.ds(_:)` for text, `DSShadow` for elevation and `DSAnimation` for motion. Never write literal numbers, fonts or colors.
5. **Colors come from the theme.** In your own views, declare `@DSThemed private var theme` and paint with its roles (table below). Don't use `DSColors.x` inside a view body; those statics don't follow the injected theme.
6. **No borders.** Separate surfaces with `.dsSurface(_:radius:)`, `DSCard`, `theme.subtleFill` or `.dsWashEdge(radius:)`. Never use `.border` or `.stroke`.
7. **Haptics are built in.** `DSButton`, `DSToggle`, `DSStepper`, `DSTabBar`, `.dsToast` and the other controls already fire their haptic. Don't add a second one. Call `dsHaptic(_:)` only for your own custom controls.
8. **Springs for touch, eased curves for ambience.** Use `DSAnimation.springSnappy` / `.springSmooth` for state changes caused by a tap or drag, and `withAnimation(DSAnimation.normal)` for theme changes. Loop effects through `.dsBreathe`, `.dsShimmer` or `DSMotion.loop(_:unless:)`, which respect Reduce Motion.
9. **Accessibility is part of the job.** Give icon-only buttons an `accessibilityLabel:`, give bare controls (`DSStepper`, `DSRating`) a `.accessibilityLabel("Guests")`, and keep text on `.ds(_:)` so it scales with Dynamic Type.
10. **Async work goes into the component.** `DSSlideToConfirm`'s `onConfirm` is `async throws`. Await the payment inside it and throw to refuse; the control spins, then succeeds or re-opens by itself.

## Component chooser

| You need | Use | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Primary / secondary action | `DSButton(_:variant:size:icon:isLoading:action:)` | `.primary` is the accent fill; one per screen. |
| Icon-only action | `DSIconButton(icon:accessibilityLabel:action:)` | Always pass `accessibilityLabel`. |
| Confirm a payment or a destructive action | `DSSlideToConfirm(_:confirmedLabel:finish:onConfirm:)` | `onConfirm` is `async throws`. |
| Confirm by holding (power off, send, one-handed) | `DSHoldToConfirm(_:icon:confirmedLabel:duration:accent:onConfirm:)` | Same `async throws` `onConfirm`; VoiceOver double-taps instead of holding. |
| On/off setting | `DSToggle(_:isOn:)` | |
| Pick any of several (terms, a todo, multi-select) | `DSCheckbox(_:isOn:size:)` | Label is tappable; box-only needs `.accessibilityLabel(…)`. |
| Small number (quantity, guests) | `DSStepper(value:in:step:)` | Add `.accessibilityLabel(…)`. |
| Pick one from a list of options (plan, payment) | `DSRadioGroup(selection:options:)` | Any `Hashable` value; wrap in `DSCard`; `.accessibilityLabel("…")` on the group. |
| Continuous value (volume, price, opacity) | `DSSlider(value:in:step:)` | `Double` binding, default `0...1`; pass `step` for notches. It draws no value: show your own read-out. Add `.accessibilityLabel(…)`. |
| A span: min and max (price filter, age, hours) | `DSRangeSlider(range:in:step:minimumDistance:)` | `ClosedRange<Double>` binding; the knobs never cross and keep `minimumDistance` apart. Draws no values: show your own read-out. Add `.accessibilityLabel(…)`. |
| Pick one of 2–4 options | `DSSegmentedControl(selection:options:)` | `style: .underline` for a tab-like look. |
| Star rating | `DSRating(rating:)` / `DSRating(value:)` (read-only) | |
| Like / favorite / bookmark toggle | `DSLikeButton(isLiked:count:symbol:emptySymbol:accessibilityLabel:)` | Pops and radiates a halo when a tap likes. Pass `accessibilityLabel:` that matches a swapped symbol (default "Like"); `count` is display-only, so update it in `.onChange(of: isLiked)`. |
| Text input | `DSTextField(label:placeholder:icon:text:state:)` | `DSSearchBar(text:)` for search. |
| One-time code | `DSCodeField(code:state:onComplete:)` | SMS autofill on iOS. |
| Amount, passcode or quantity without the system keyboard | `DSKeypad(text:maxLength:decimalPlaces:)` | Edits a `String`; `decimalPlaces: 2` for money (locale separator), `0` for a PIN. It draws no value: show your own read-out with an `accessibilityLabel`. |
| App sections at the bottom | `DSTabBar(selection:items:)` | Place with `.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)`. |
| Horizontal paging content | `DSCarousel(_:currentPage:content:)` + `DSPageControl` | |
| Page dots | `DSPageControl(currentPage:numberOfPages:)` | |
| Modal panel | `.dsSheet(isPresented:detents:content:)` | Native sheet with Velvet chrome. |
| A surface to group content | `DSCard { … }` | `DSInteractiveCard(action:)` when tappable. |
| Expandable section, FAQ row | `DSDisclosureGroup(_:subtitle:icon:initiallyExpanded:content:)` | Use this, not the stock `DisclosureGroup`. `isExpanded:` instead of `initiallyExpanded:` for state you own (accordion). |
| Rows in a group | `DSListCell(title:subtitle:leading:trailing:action:)` + `DSDivider` | Inside `DSCard(padding: 0)`. |
| Status label / unread count | `DSBadge(_:variant:)`, `DSCountBadge(count:)` | |
| Person | `DSAvatar(name:imageURL:size:)` | Falls back to initials. |
| Transient message | `.dsToast($toast, edge:)` with `DSToastValue(_:type:duration:)` | Slides in, fires its haptic, auto-dismisses, flicks away, announces itself. `DSToast(_:type:)` is the bare banner. |
| Nothing to show | `DSEmptyState(icon:title:message:actionTitle:action:)` | |
| Loading layout | `.dsSkeleton(isLoading)` or `DSSkeleton` blocks | |
| Progress | `DSCircularProgress`, `DSLinearProgress`, `DSGradientProgress`, `DSStepProgress` | |
| Animated number | `DSNumberTicker(_:format:)` (rolling digits), `DSAnimatedNumber` (count-up) | |
| Trend / small chart | `DSSparkline(_:)`, `DSBarChart(_:labels:selection:)` | Use Swift Charts for axes, legends, many series. |
| Success moment | `DSSuccessCheck(isComplete:)`, `.dsConfetti(trigger:)` | Confetti is decorative; pair it with a real result. |
| AI / background work | `DSThinkingIndicator(phrases:)` | |
| Typed headline | `DSTypewriterText(_:style:)` | |
| Rows or cards that recede at the scroll edge | `.dsScrollReveal(_:)` | On each repeated item inside a `ScrollView`; rests under Reduce Motion. |
| Ambient motion on any view | `.dsBreathe()`, `.dsJiggle(trigger:)`, `.dsPopIn(delay:)`, `.dsEdgeSweep()`, `.dsHueDrift()` | |
| Menu, context menu | SwiftUI `Menu`, `.contextMenu` | Native is right; it inherits the tint. |
| Pull to refresh | `.refreshable { await … }` | Native. |
| Tips, coach marks | TipKit | Native. |
| Alerts, confirmations | `.alert`, `.confirmationDialog` | Native. |
| Date and time input | `DatePicker` | Native, tinted with `.tint(theme.ink)`. |

## Tokens cheat sheet

**Theme roles** (from `@DSThemed private var theme`):

| Role | Use for |
|---|---|
| `theme.accent` | Fills: primary CTA, toggle on, selected tab, active indicator |
| `theme.onAccent` | Text and icons **on** `theme.accent` |
| `theme.ink` | Text, icons, links and focus **on glass or surfaces** |
| `theme.palette.textPrimary` / `.textSecondary` / `.textTertiary` | Body copy hierarchy |
| `theme.palette.success` / `.warning` / `.error` / `.info` | Status; `theme.palette.textOnPrimary` for text on them |
| `theme.subtleFill` | Flat fill for a surface nested in another |
| `theme.backgroundColor` / `theme.style.background` | The flat page tone behind a screen |

**Spacing** (`DSSpacing`, 4 pt grid): `xxxs` 2 · `xxs` 4 · `xs` 8 · `sm` 12 · `md` 16 · `lg` 20 · `xl` 24 · `xxl` 32 · `xxxl` 40 · `huge` 48 · `massive` 64. Screen margin: `.dsScreenPadding()` (20).

**Radius by role** (`DSRadius`): `.card` 20 (cards, sheets) · `.surface` 16 (nested surfaces) · `.control` 12 (buttons, inputs) · `.chip` pill (badges, small buttons).

**Text** (`Text("…").ds(.style)` or `.dsTextStyle(.style)`): `hero`, `largeTitle`, `title1`, `title2`, `title3`, `body`, `callout`, `footnote`, `caption1`, `caption2`, `button`, `buttonSmall`, `overline`, `displayLarge`, `displayMedium`, `numeric`, `badge`. Pass a color with `.ds(.callout, color: theme.palette.textSecondary)`.

**Surfaces** (`.dsSurface(_:radius:)`): `.glassThin` (chips, toolbars) · `.glass` (cards, default) · `.glassThick` (sheets, popovers) · `.solid`. They fall back to solid under Reduce Transparency.

**Shadows** (`.dsShadow(_:)`): `.sm`, `.md`, `.lg`, `.xl`, `.glow(theme.accent)` (primary CTA only).

**Motion** (`DSAnimation`): `micro` 0.20 s, `fast` 0.24 s, `normal` 0.32 s, `slow` 0.48 s curves; springs `springSnappy`, `springSmooth`, `springGentle`, `springBouncy`; `ambient` for loops. Press feel: `DSPress.scale` (0.96) with `DSPress.animation`.

**Haptics** (`dsHaptic(_:)`): `.light`, `.medium`, `.heavy`, `.soft`, `.rigid`, `.selection`, `.success`, `.warning`, `.error`. No-op on macOS.

All values: [docs/tokens.md](docs/tokens.md).

## Patterns

Every snippet below compiles against the current API (they're mirrored in the test suite).

**A screen**

```swift
struct ProfileScreen: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xl) {
                Text("Profile").ds(.largeTitle)
                DSCard {
                    HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                        DSAvatar(name: "Ada Lovelace", size: 56)
                        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xxs) {
                            Text("Ada Lovelace").ds(.title3)
                            Text("Member since 2024").ds(.footnote)
                        }
                        Spacer()
                    }
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

**A settings group**

```swift
struct NotificationSettings: View {
    @State private var push = true
    @State private var digest = false

    var body: some View {
        DSCard(padding: 0) {
            VStack(spacing: 0) {
                DSListCell(title: "Push notifications") {
                    Image(systemName: "bell")
                } trailing: {
                    DSToggle(isOn: $push)
                }
                DSDivider(inset: DSSpacing.md)
                DSListCell(title: "Weekly digest", subtitle: "Every Monday") {
                    Image(systemName: "envelope")
                } trailing: {
                    DSToggle(isOn: $digest)
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**A primary action pinned to the bottom**

```swift
struct CheckoutScreen: View {
    @State private var isPaying = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            Text("Your order").ds(.largeTitle).dsScreenPadding()
        }
        .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) {
            DSButton("Pay $24.00", size: .large, isFullWidth: true, isLoading: isPaying) {
                isPaying = true
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

**An async confirmation**

```swift
struct PayRow: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSSlideToConfirm("Slide to pay $24.00", confirmedLabel: "Paid", finish: .morphAndVanish) {
            try await PaymentService.charge(cents: 2400)   // throw to refuse; the control re-opens
        }
    }
}

enum PaymentService {
    static func charge(cents: Int) async throws { try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1)) }
}
```

**Loading, then content**

```swift
struct ArticleCard: View {
    @State private var isLoading = true

    var body: some View {
        DSCard {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                Text("Weekend in Lisbon").ds(.title3)
                Text("Three nights by the river, two guests.").ds(.callout)
            }
            .dsSkeleton(isLoading)
        }
        .task {
            try? await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
            isLoading = false
        }
    }
}
```

Keep `.task` and `.onAppear` outside the view you pass to `.dsSkeleton`.

**A tab bar shell**

```swift
enum AppTab: Hashable { case home, search, inbox, profile }

struct AppShell: View {
    @State private var tab = AppTab.home

    var body: some View {
        Group {
            switch tab {
            case .home:    Text("Home").ds(.largeTitle)
            case .search:  Text("Search").ds(.largeTitle)
            case .inbox:   Text("Inbox").ds(.largeTitle)
            case .profile: Text("Profile").ds(.largeTitle)
            }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .dsBackdrop()
        .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) {
            DSTabBar(selection: $tab, items: [
                DSTabItem("Home", value: .home, icon: "house", selectedIcon: "house.fill"),
                DSTabItem("Search", value: .search, icon: "magnifyingglass"),
                DSTabItem("Inbox", value: .inbox, icon: "tray", selectedIcon: "tray.fill", badge: 3),
                DSTabItem("Profile", value: .profile, icon: "person", selectedIcon: "person.fill"),
            ])
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

**A toast**

```swift
struct SaveButton: View {
    @State private var toast: DSToastValue?

    var body: some View {
        DSButton("Save") {
            toast = DSToastValue("Saved to your library", type: .success)
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .dsToast($toast, edge: .bottom)
    }
}
```

Assign a new value to replace the toast on screen (the timer restarts); assign `nil` to dismiss. `duration: 0` keeps it up until you clear it.

**Your own view, on-system**

```swift
struct PriceTag: View {
    let amount: String
    @DSThemed private var theme

    var body: some View {
        Text(amount)
            .ds(.numeric, color: theme.onAccent)
            .padding(.horizontal, DSSpacing.sm)
            .padding(.vertical, DSSpacing.xxs)
            .background(theme.accent, in: Capsule())
    }
}
```

**Switching the theme at runtime**

```swift
struct ThemePicker: View {
    let theme: DSTheme

    var body: some View {
        DSSegmentedControl(
            selection: Binding(
                get: { theme.style.id },
                set: { id in
                    withAnimation(DSAnimation.normal) {
                        theme.style = DSThemeStyle.all.first { $0.id == id } ?? .sunset
                    }
                }
            ),
            segments: DSThemeStyle.all.map { DSSegment($0.name, value: $0.id) }
        )
    }
}
```

## Anti-patterns

| Don't | Do | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `.foregroundStyle(.blue)`, `Color(hex: "FF7E5F")` in a view | `theme.ink`, `theme.accent`, `theme.palette.textSecondary` | Literals ignore the theme and dark mode. |
| `DSColors.primary` inside `body` | `@DSThemed private var theme` then `theme.accent` | Statics don't follow the injected theme. |
| `.font(.system(size: 17))`, `.font(.headline)` | `.ds(.body)`, `.ds(.title3)` | DS styles carry tracking, line spacing and Dynamic Type. |
| `.padding(15)`, `.cornerRadius(10)` | `.padding(DSSpacing.md)`, `.dsSurface(.glass, radius: DSRadius.control)` | Off-grid values drift from the system. |
| `.border(.gray)`, `.overlay(RoundedRectangle(…).stroke(…))` | `.dsSurface(_:radius:)`, `.dsWashEdge(radius:)`, `theme.subtleFill` | Velvet has no borders. |
| `DSCard { DSCard { … } }` | Inner `DSCard(style: .flat)` or `.background(theme.subtleFill)` | Glass on glass turns muddy. |
| A haptic in the action of a `DSButton` | Nothing. The button already fires one. | Double haptics feel broken. |
| `withAnimation(.easeInOut)` after a tap | `withAnimation(DSAnimation.springSnappy)` | Touch gets springs. |
| `.repeatForever()` on your own loop | `.dsBreathe()` or `DSMotion.loop(_:unless: reduceMotion)` | Loops must rest under Reduce Motion. |
| `ScrollView { DSScreen { … } }` | `DSScreen(backdrop: true) { … }` alone | `DSScreen` already scrolls. |
| Overlaying a bare `DSToast` and timing it yourself | `.dsToast($toast)` with a `DSToastValue` | The presenter handles the timer, replacement, haptic and flick to dismiss. |
| `Image(systemName: "trash")` as a button with no label | `DSIconButton(icon: "trash", accessibilityLabel: "Delete") { … }` | VoiceOver reads "trash" or nothing. |
| A `DSStepper` with no label | `.accessibilityLabel("Guests")` | It reads "Stepper" otherwise. |
| `DSListCell(title: "Wi-Fi") { Image(systemName: "wifi") }` | `DSListCell(title: "Wi-Fi", leading: { Image(systemName: "wifi") })` | A single trailing closure binds to `action`, so the icon never shows. |
| Adding the package **and** copying sources | Pick one | Duplicate symbols. |
| Glass on a plain white screen, then "it looks flat" | `DSScreen(backdrop: true)` or `.dsBackdrop()` | Glass needs something behind it. |

## Naming

- Types start with `DS` (`DSButton`, `DSTabItem`); modifiers start with `ds` (`.dsSurface`, `.dsConfetti`).
- Bindings: `selection:` for a selected value, `value:` / `isOn:` / `rating:` / `code:` / `text:` for edited values, `currentPage:` for page indices.
- Optional tint parameters are `Color? = nil` (`accent:`, `color:`, `tint:`); `nil` means "follow the theme". Passing `nil` explicitly is fine.
- `haptic:` is the parameter for a configurable haptic, `accessibilityLabel:` for VoiceOver text, and the trailing closure is `action:`, `content:` or `onConfirm:`.

## Before you hand back

- Build for every platform the app targets. `swift build` alone only checks macOS.
- Look at the screen in light and dark mode, with the theme injected, on a backdrop.
- Turn on Reduce Motion and check that the UI still makes sense at rest.
- Search your diff for `Color(`, `.font(.system`, `.stroke(`, `.border(`, `cornerRadius(` and literal numbers in `padding`. Each one is usually a missed token.

## Working on Velvet UI itself

Library code follows the rules in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): tokens only, colors from `@DSThemed`, `Color? = nil` for overridable colors, no borders, `DSPress` for press states, both platforms building, and a definition of done that includes docs, a Gallery stage and the registry entry. [docs/engineering-notes.md](docs/engineering-notes.md) records the decisions and gotchas.

---
<!-- source: docs/tokens.md -->

# Tokens reference

Every value a component is allowed to use. If you need something that isn't here, add a token first, then use it. Files live in `Sources/VelvetUI/Tokens/`, `Animation/`, `Haptics/`, `Layout/`.

## Theme

`DSTheme` (`Tokens/DSTheme.swift`) is an `@Observable` class holding `light`, `dark` (`DSColorPalette`) and `style` (`DSThemeStyle`). Inject once with `.dsTheme(theme)`. When nothing is injected, a shared default (Sunset) is used.

Inside views, read it with the property wrapper:

```swift
@DSThemed private var theme        // DSResolvedTheme for the current color scheme
theme.palette.textPrimary          // neutrals & status colors
theme.accent / theme.onAccent      // fills and their text
theme.ink                          // text / icons / focus on glass, resolved light/dark
theme.backgroundColor              // the flat page tone for the current scheme
theme.subtleFill                   // wash on a backdrop, backgroundSecondary otherwise
theme.washSurface / theme.washEdge // raw wash values
theme.isDark / theme.onBackdrop
```

`DSResolvedTheme` is a value type; `DSTheme.resolved(for:onBackdrop:)` builds one without a view.

## Theme styles

`DSThemeStyle` (`Tokens/DSThemeStyle.swift`). A style is a solid page background (`DSBackground`) plus four derived colors, each with one job. Contrast is verified by `VelvetUITests.testThemeStylesMeetAAContrast`.

| Style | Background | `accent` | `onAccent` | `ink` | `inkDark` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.sunset` (default) | Paper `#FAF8F4` / `#121110` | `#FF7E5F` | `#2B1510` | `#C2361A` | `#FFA98F` |
| `.aurora` | Snow `#FFFFFF` / `#000000` | `#7F5AF0` | `#FFFFFF` | `#6D47E6` | `#B9A3FF` |
| `.lagoon` | Graphite `#F0F0F2` / `#1B1C1E` | `#16F2B3` | `#06231D` | `#0A7382` | `#5EF5CB` |

| Slot | Use it for | Contrast rule |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | The flat page tone drawn by `DSBackdrop` | — |
| `accent` | Primary CTA fill, toggle on, active page dot, filled badge, progress fills | — |
| `onAccent` | Text and icons on `accent` | ≥ 4.5:1 on accent |
| `ink` | Text, icons, links, focus glow on light glass | ≥ 4.5:1 on the light page tone |
| `inkDark` | Same, on dark glass | ≥ 4.5:1 on the dark page tone |

Custom styles: `DSThemeStyle(id:name:background:accent:onAccent:ink:inkDark:)`. Keep the contrast rules or text on glass becomes unreadable. `DSThemeStyle.all` lists the built-ins for pickers.

## Backgrounds

`DSBackground` (`Tokens/DSBackground.swift`). Velvet ships **no background gradients**: a page is one flat tone per scheme. The built-in tones are deliberately neutral so the accent is the only color on screen.

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.snow` | `#FFFFFF` | `#000000` | True monochrome; maximum contrast, OLED-friendly dark |
| `.paper` | `#FAF8F4` | `#121110` | Warm off-white and warm black; pairs with coral and amber |
| `.graphite` | `#F0F0F2` | `#1B1C1E` | Cool light grey and graphite; pairs with violet and teal |

Custom backgrounds: `DSBackground(id:name:light:dark:)`. `DSBackground.all` lists the built-ins. Every style must point at a shipped background so `VelvetUITests.testBuiltInStylesAreDistinct` can check it.

## Colors

`DSColorPalette` (`Tokens/DSColors.swift`) holds neutrals and status colors. 19 slots, memberwise `init`. Don't add slots (it would break every custom palette); add a new type instead.

| Slot | Light | Dark | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `primary` / `primaryVariant` | `#FF7E5F` / `#C2361A` | `#FF7E5F` / `#FFA98F` | Mirrors Sunset accent / ink for raw-token code |
| `secondary` / `secondaryVariant` | `#7F5AF0` / `#6D47E6` | `#7F5AF0` / `#B9A3FF` | Secondary button fill |
| `tertiary` | `#16F2B3` | `#16F2B3` | Accent alternative |
| `success` / `warning` / `error` / `info` | `#22C55E` / `#F59E0B` / `#EF4444` / `#3B82F6` | `#34D399` / `#FBBF24` / `#F87171` / `#60A5FA` | Status |
| `backgroundPrimary` / `Secondary` / `Elevated` | `#FFFFFF` / `#F7F7F7` / `#FFFFFF` | `#0F0F1A` / `#1A1A2E` / `#242440` | Screens, subtle fills, solid surface fallback |
| `textPrimary` / `Secondary` / `Tertiary` | `#1A1A2E` / `#6B7280` / `#9CA3AF` | `#F9FAFB` / `#9CA3AF` / `#6B7280` | Text hierarchy |
| `textOnPrimary` | `#FFFFFF` | `#FFFFFF` | Text on **secondary, status, destructive** fills. On the accent use `onAccent`. |
| `border` / `borderFocused` / `divider` | `#E5E7EB` / `#C2361A` / `#F3F4F6` | `#374151` / `#FFA98F` / `#1F2937` | Legacy separators and inactive tracks. Components should prefer `subtleFill` / `ink`. |

`DSColors.primary`, `DSColors.textPrimary`, … are **adaptive light/dark** static colors built from the two default palettes (`Color.dsDynamic(light:dark:)`). Use them in previews, models, or quick prototypes. They do not follow a custom injected palette — inside views use `@DSThemed`.

`Color(hex:)` accepts `RRGGBB` or `AARRGGBB`, with or without `#`.

## Surfaces

`DSSurface` (`Tokens/DSSurface.swift`) + `.dsSurface(_ level, radius:, edge:)`.

| Level | Material | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `.glassThin` | `ultraThinMaterial` | Chips, toolbars, small floating elements; `DSStepper` and `DSSlideToConfirm` tracks |
| `.glass` | `thinMaterial` | **Cards (default)**, list groups |
| `.glassThick` | `regularMaterial` | Sheets, modals, popovers, outlined cards |
| `.solid` | `backgroundElevated` | Fallback; also what every level becomes under Reduce Transparency |

The modifier fills, clips to a continuous rounded rect and draws `DSWash.edge` inside the shape. Default radius `DSRadius.card`.

## Wash

`DSWash` (`Tokens/DSWash.swift`). Velvet never calls `.stroke()` with a border color.

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `surface(for:)` | white 0.45 | white 0.10 | Flat translucent fill for a surface nested inside another, such as the flat card. Read via `theme.washSurface`, or `theme.subtleFill` for the no-backdrop fallback. |
| `edge(for:)` | white 0.55 → 0.05, top → bottom | white 0.18 → 0.02 | 1pt specular highlight (`edgeWidth`), drawn with `strokeBorder`. `.dsWashEdge(radius:)` |
| focus | opacity 0.35, width 2, blur 1.5 | same | `.dsFocusGlow(color, radius:, isActive:)` — pass `theme.ink` or a status color |

## Backdrop

`DSBackdrop` (`Layout/DSBackdrop.swift`) fills the screen with the active style's solid page tone — no gradient, no radial light, no dim layer. Wrap style changes in `withAnimation(DSAnimation.normal)` for a crossfade.

`.dsBackdrop()` puts it behind a view **and** sets `EnvironmentValues.dsOnBackdrop = true`, which is how `theme.subtleFill` knows to use the wash. `DSScreen(backdrop: true)` does this for a whole screen.

## Shadows

`DSShadow` (`Tokens/DSShadow.swift`) + `.dsShadow(_:)`. Radius / opacity / y-offset.

| Level | Values | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `.sm` | 8 / 0.04 / 2 | Toggle knob, active segment |
| `.md` | 16 / 0.06 / 4 | Cards at rest |
| `.lg` | 24 / 0.08 / 8 | Toast, popovers |
| `.xl` | 32 / 0.10 / 12 | Sheets, modals |
| `.glow(tint)` | 20 / 0.28 light · 0.40 dark / 8 | Primary CTA, toggle on. Pass `theme.accent`. |

Shadow color is black except for `.glow`. `color(for:)` is scheme-aware; the modifier uses it.

## Radius

`DSRadius` (`Tokens/DSRadius.swift`). Always continuous corners.

| Numeric | Value | Semantic alias | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xs` | 4 | | |
| `sm` | 8 | | |
| `md` | 12 | `control` | Buttons medium/large, inputs, code-field boxes, toast |
| `lg` | 16 | `surface` | Nested surfaces, such as a flat card inside a card |
| `xl` | 20 | `card` | DSCard, DSInteractiveCard, DSImageCard, sheets |
| `xxl` | 24 | | Hero cards |
| `pill` | 9999 | `chip` | Badges, tags, small buttons, search bar, segmented pill |

`.dsCornerRadius(_:)` clips. The stroke overload is deprecated.

### Corners (`DSCorner`)

`DSCorner` (`Tokens/DSCorner.swift`) says how a shape rounds its corners. Apple's corner concentricity (iOS / macOS 26) sits behind it: a concentric corner shares its centre with the container's corner, so **inner radius = container radius − distance**, and the gap between the two curves stays even.

| Case / token | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `.fixed(r)` | always `r` | Anything that must not change shape |
| `.concentric(minimum:)` | follows the container, never under `minimum` | Shapes that sit inside something |
| `.card` | `.fixed(DSRadius.card)` | First-level cards |
| `.nestedSurface` | `.concentric(minimum: DSRadius.surface)` | A card inside a card or a sheet |
| `.control` | `.concentric(minimum: DSRadius.control)` | DSButton medium/large, DSTextField, DSToast, the DSRadioGroup highlight |
| `.chip` | `.fixed(DSRadius.chip)` | Pills |

- **Containers:** `dsSurface`, every `DSCard` style and `.dsContainer(radius:)` publish their shape to what's inside. The system does it for sheets, popovers and the screen corners.
- **Fallback:** below iOS / macOS 26, without a container, or for corners far from the container's corners, a concentric corner uses `minimum`. On older systems Velvet looks exactly as it did.
- **At Velvet's scale** (card 20, padding 16) the concentric radius inside a card is 4, so `minimum` wins and controls stay at 12. The difference shows in large containers: sheets, the screen corners, and surfaces with tight padding.
- API: `corner.shape` (an `AnyShape` to fill, clip or stroke), `dsSurface(_:corner:edge:)`, `dsWashEdge(corner:)`, `dsFocusGlow(_:corner:isActive:)`, `DSCard(style:padding:corner:)`. The `radius:` overloads are unchanged and mean `.fixed`.

## Spacing

`DSSpacing` (`Tokens/DSSpacing.swift`), 4pt grid: `xxxs` 2 · `xxs` 4 · `xs` 8 · `sm` 12 · `md` 16 · `lg` 20 · `xl` 24 · `xxl` 32 · `xxxl` 40 · `huge` 48 · `massive` 64. Screen margins: `screenHorizontal` 20, `screenHorizontalCompact` 16, `screenTop` 16, `screenBottom` 24. Helpers: `.dsScreenPadding()`, `.dsPadding(_:)`, `.dsPadding(horizontal:vertical:)`.

## Typography

`DSTextStyle` (`Tokens/DSTypography.swift`). Apply with `Text("…").ds(.title1)` or `.dsTextStyle(.body, color:)`. Color defaults to `theme.palette.textPrimary`.

| Style | Size / weight | Design | Tracking | Use |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hero` | 34 bold | SF Pro | −0.8 | Onboarding headlines |
| `largeTitle` | 28 bold | SF Pro | −0.6 | Screen titles |
| `title1` | 22 semibold | SF Pro | −0.4 | Section headers |
| `title2` | 20 semibold | SF Pro | −0.3 | Card titles |
| `title3` | 17 semibold | SF Pro | −0.2 | Subsection headers |
| `body` | 17 regular | SF Pro | 0 | Body text |
| `callout` | 15 regular | SF Pro | 0 | Secondary content |
| `footnote` | 13 medium | SF Pro | 0 | Labels, metadata |
| `caption1` / `caption2` | 12 / 11 regular | SF Pro | 0 | Timestamps / fine print |
| `button` / `buttonSmall` | 15 / 13 semibold | Rounded | 0 | Button labels |
| `overline` | 11 bold, uppercase | SF Pro | +1.2 | Section overlines |
| `displayLarge` / `displayMedium` | 60 / 40 bold | Rounded, monospaced digits | −1.2 / −0.6 | Stats, timers |
| `numeric` | 17 semibold | Rounded, monospaced digits | 0 | Prices, counters inline |
| `badge` | 11 bold | Rounded | 0 | Count badges |

**Dynamic Type.** `.ds(_:)` / `.dsTextStyle(_:)` scale with the user's text size: each style scales along a system text style (`DSTextStyle.textStyle`, e.g. `body` -> `.body`, `hero` -> `.largeTitle`) via `@ScaledMetric`, and line spacing scales too. At the default size the output is identical to the old fixed fonts. `DSTextStyle.size/weight/design/textStyle` are public. `.dsFont(_:)` applies only the scaled font (no color, tracking or line spacing); `DSTextStyle.font` stays fixed-size. Some controls still use fixed fonts: DSButton, the input text of DSTextField / DSSearchBar, DSSegmentedControl and DSBadge / DSCountBadge. DSStepper (number), DSCodeField (digits) and DSSlideToConfirm (label) use `.ds(_:)` and scale, but their boxes and tracks have fixed heights.

Rule: numbers are always Rounded; titles are never Rounded. Max three styles per visual section.

## Motion

`DSAnimation` (`Animation/DSAnimation.swift`).

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `micro` | 0.20s, curve (0.25, 0.10, 0.25, 1) | Toggles, highlights, color changes |
| `fast` | 0.24s, curve (0.20, 0, 0, 1) | State changes, button feedback |
| `normal` | 0.32s, curve (0.20, 0, 0, 1) | View transitions, card reveals, theme crossfade |
| `slow` | 0.48s, curve (0.30, 0, 0.10, 1) | Large layout shifts |
| `springSnappy` | response 0.3, damping 0.7 | Buttons, toggles, press states |
| `springSmooth` | 0.45 / 0.75 | Cards, panels |
| `springGentle` | 0.6 / 0.8 | Sheets, full-screen |
| `springBouncy` | 0.5 / 0.5 | Celebrations, rating pop |
| `interactive` | 0.3 / 0.7, blend 0.05 | Gesture-driven |
| `progress` / `counting` | easeInOut 0.8 / easeOut 1.0 | Progress fills / number count-up |
| `ambient` | easeInOut 1.8s | Base curve for ambient loops (breathe, drift, sweep) |
| `stagger(index:base:)` | springSmooth + index × 0.05s | List entrances |

`DSPress`: `scale` 0.96, `iconScale` 0.88, `animation` = springSnappy. Every pressable component uses these.

Transitions: `.dsSlideUp`, `.dsScale`, `.dsFade`, `.dsPush`. Modifiers: `.dsAnimate(_:value:)`, `.dsStaggerIn(index:)` (fade + 8pt rise, respects Reduce Motion), `.dsShimmer()`, `.dsPulse()` (deprecated — use `.dsBreathe()`).

### Motion primitives

These live in `Animation/DSMotion.swift` and are the ambient layer above `DSAnimation`, composing constant motion effects for decorative and attention-holding purposes.

| Modifier | What it does | Reduce Motion |
|---|---|---|
| `.dsBreathe(_ intensity:)` | Slow swell in scale and dip in opacity at `breatheDuration` | Rests at scale 1 |
| `.dsJiggle(trigger:)` | One decaying shake on trigger change — a continuous keyframe track through `jiggleSwings`, ending at rest | Not applied at all |
| `.dsPopIn(delay:)` | Entrance with springBouncy overshoot and fade | Fades only, no scale |
| `.dsEdgeSweep(radius:isActive:)` | Specular highlight travelling the surface edge | Highlight stays static |
| `.dsHueDrift(isActive:)` | Slow, bounded hue rotation over the accent (decorative) | Stays at 0° |
| `.dsScrollReveal(_ intensity:)` | Scale and opacity follow the scroll position (`Animation/DSScrollEffects.swift`) | Full presence, no change |

`DSMotion.loop(_:autoreverses:unless:)` wraps an animation in `repeatForever`, or returns `nil` when Reduce Motion is on. Passing nil to `.animation(_:value:)` applies the change instantly, so every ambient effect settles at its resting state instead of being skipped.

| Constant | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `breatheDuration` | 2.4s | Breathing swell. Slow enough to read as alive, not as a spinner. |
| `sweepDuration` | 2.0s | One full trip of the edge sweep. |
| `driftDuration` | 8.0s | Hue drift. Deliberately slow: notice it only on a second look. |
| `driftDegrees` | 12 | Maximum hue rotation. Small to keep the accent recognisable. |
| `jiggleDegrees` | 7 | Peak rotation of the first jiggle swing; later swings shrink from here. |
| `jiggleDuration` | 0.45s | Total length of one jiggle — a quick "no" shake. |
| `jiggleSwings` | `[7, -4.34, 2.66, -1.26, 0]` | The decay envelope in degrees; Cubic keyframes interpolate between the points. |
| `scrollRevealSubtleScale` / `…MediumScale` / `…StrongScale` | 0.96 / 0.90 / 0.80 | Scale of `.dsScrollReveal` once the view is fully past the scroll view edge. |
| `scrollRevealSubtleOpacity` / `…MediumOpacity` / `…StrongOpacity` | 0.65 / 0.40 / 0.15 | Opacity of `.dsScrollReveal` at the edge. |

## Haptics

`DSHapticStyle` (`Haptics/DSHaptics.swift`): `light`, `medium`, `heavy`, `soft`, `rigid`, `selection`, `success`, `warning`, `error`. Fire with `dsHaptic(.success)`, `DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.medium, intensity: 0.7)`, or `.dsHapticTap(.light) { }`. No-op on macOS. Components fire their own haptics — don't double up.

## Layout

`DSScreen(backgroundColor:backdrop:)`, `DSHorizontalScroll`, `DSVStack`, `DSHStack`, `DSGrid(minItemWidth:)` in `Layout/DSLayout.swift`.

<!-- source: docs/components/DSButton.md -->

# DSButton

A themed text button with optional icon and loading state. It presses down with a spring and taps out a haptic, so every action feels acknowledged.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSButton.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSButton.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ButtonDemo: View {
    @State private var isSaving = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                DSButton("Save changes", icon: "checkmark", isFullWidth: true, isLoading: isSaving) {
                    isSaving = true
                }
                DSButton("Cancel", variant: .ghost) { }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `String` | required | Button text (unlabeled first argument). |
| `variant` | `DSButtonVariant` | `.primary` | `.primary`, `.secondary`, `.outline`, `.ghost` or `.destructive`. |
| `size` | `DSButtonSize` | `.medium` | `.small` (36pt pill), `.medium` (44pt), `.large` (52pt). |
| `icon` | `String?` | `nil` | SF Symbol name shown beside the title. |
| `iconPosition` | `IconPosition` | `.leading` | `.leading` or `.trailing`. |
| `isFullWidth` | `Bool` | `false` | Stretch to the available width. |
| `isLoading` | `Bool` | `false` | Shows a spinner, dims the button and disables taps. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.medium` | Haptic fired on tap. |
| `action` | `() -> Void` | required | Called on tap (trailing closure). |

Icon-only buttons use [`DSIconButton`](DSIconButton.md).

## Variants

| Variant | Look |
|---|---|
| `.primary` | Theme accent fill, `onAccent` text. |
| `.secondary` | Palette secondary fill. |
| `.outline` | Clear fill with an ink outline. |
| `.ghost` | Text only, no fill. |
| `.destructive` | Error-red fill for irreversible actions. |

```swift
struct ButtonVariantsDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
            DSButton("Primary") { }
            DSButton("Secondary", variant: .secondary) { }
            DSButton("Outline", variant: .outline) { }
            DSButton("Ghost", variant: .ghost) { }
            DSButton("Delete account", variant: .destructive, icon: "trash") { }
            DSButton("Next", size: .large, icon: "arrow.right", iconPosition: .trailing) { }
            DSButton("Tag", size: .small) { }
        }
    }
}
```

`.small` is a pill; `.medium` and `.large` use the control corner radius.

## Behavior

- Pressing scales the button down with the shared press spring and releases back on lift.
- A haptic fires on tap (`.medium` by default; pass `haptic:` to change it). Don't add another at the call site.
- While `isLoading` is true the button shows a spinner, dims to 80% and ignores taps.

## Accessibility

- VoiceOver reads the button as a standard SwiftUI `Button` whose label is `title`; the icon is decorative. While loading it is disabled and read as dimmed.
- Override the spoken label from outside with `.accessibilityLabel("Save your changes")`.
- Label text doesn't scale with Dynamic Type yet: the control has a fixed height, so its label keeps a fixed size. Text elsewhere on your screen that uses `.ds(_:)` / `.dsTextStyle(_:)` does scale.

## See also

- [DSIconButton](DSIconButton.md)
- [DSSlideToConfirm](DSSlideToConfirm.md)
- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSIconButton.md -->

# DSIconButton

An icon-only button, with no background, that shrinks under your thumb and ticks a light haptic. Use it for toolbar-style actions like share, favorite and more.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSButton.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSButton.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct IconButtonDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                DSIconButton(icon: "square.and.arrow.up", accessibilityLabel: "Share") { }
                DSIconButton(icon: "heart", haptic: .medium, accessibilityLabel: "Favorite") { }
                DSIconButton(icon: "ellipsis", size: 36, accessibilityLabel: "More options") { }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `icon` | `String` | required | SF Symbol name. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `44` | Width and height of the square tappable area in points. The symbol is drawn at 40% of it. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Icon color. Defaults to the palette's primary text color. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.light` | Haptic fired on tap. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `String?` | `nil` | What VoiceOver reads, e.g. "Share". When nil, VoiceOver falls back to the SF Symbol's own description. |
| `action` | `() -> Void` | required | Called on tap (trailing closure). |

`DSIconButton` lives in `DSButton.swift`.

## Variants

There are no style variants; adjust `size`, `color` and `haptic`:

```swift
DSIconButton(icon: "trash", size: 52, color: Color.red, haptic: .warning, accessibilityLabel: "Delete") { }
```

## Behavior

- Press uses the stronger icon press scale (shrinks more than a text button) with the shared press spring.
- A `.light` haptic fires on tap by default.

## Accessibility

- The button has no visible text, so always pass `accessibilityLabel:` (e.g. "Share"). Without it VoiceOver falls back to the SF Symbol's own description, which is often unhelpful (for example "ellipsis").
- You can also set it from outside with `.accessibilityLabel("Share")`.
- Keep `size` at 44pt or more for a comfortable touch target.

## See also

- [DSButton](DSButton.md)
- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSSlideToConfirm.md -->

# DSSlideToConfirm

A slide-to-confirm gate for irreversible actions like payments. The label dissolves under your finger, motes trail the knob, and the result lands with a success or refusal haptic.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSlideToConfirm.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSlideToConfirm.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SlideToConfirmDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                Text("Pay $24.00").ds(.title2)
                DSSlideToConfirm("Slide to pay", confirmedLabel: "Paid") {
                    try await chargeCard(amountCents: 2400)
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }

    // Stand-in for your payment call. Throwing re-opens the slider for a retry.
    private func chargeCard(amountCents: Int) async throws {
        try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `String` | required | Text on the track (unlabeled first argument). |
| `icon` | `String` | `"chevron.right"` | SF Symbol on the knob. |
| `confirmedLabel` | `String` | `"Confirmed"` | Text shown once the action succeeds. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Knob fill. Defaults to the theme accent. The trail is always the accent. |
| `finish` | `DSSlideFinish` | `.settle` | What happens after success: `.settle` or `.morphAndVanish`. |
| `onConfirm` | `() async throws -> Void` | required | Runs when the slide commits. Throwing counts as a refusal. |

A plain synchronous `() -> Void` closure also compiles, since it is a subtype of `() async throws -> Void`.

## Variants

- `.settle` (default): the control stays in place showing a check and `confirmedLabel`. Right for destructive confirmations where the screen doesn't change.
- `.morphAndVanish`: the pill collapses to a circle, resolves, then dissolves. It keeps its slot so your layout doesn't jump; swap in your own success state.

```swift
struct SlideToConfirmVanishDemo: View {
    @State private var paid = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                if paid {
                    Text("Payment received").ds(.title2)
                } else {
                    DSSlideToConfirm("Slide to pay", finish: .morphAndVanish) {
                        try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
                        paid = true
                    }
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

There is no reset API; re-mount with `.id(attempt)` to run it again.

## Behavior

- The knob follows your finger 1:1, with soft detent ticks along the track. Crossing 75% of the travel fires a rigid haptic once.
- Release before the threshold and the knob springs back with a light haptic.
- While `onConfirm` runs a spinner shows for at least half a second (applied after the closure returns, never padding a slow call). Success fires a success haptic.
- If `onConfirm` throws, an error haptic fires and the control re-opens for a retry. It never words the failure; telling the user why is your job.
- Reduce Motion: the per-letter label stagger becomes a single fade. Reduce Motion or Reduce Transparency removes the motes.

## Accessibility

- One element, read as a button with the `label` you passed and the hint "Double-tap to confirm". VoiceOver users confirm with a double-tap, no dragging.
- Value is "Processing" while `onConfirm` runs, then the `confirmedLabel` once done.
- Override the label with `.accessibilityLabel("Pay 24 dollars")` on the outside.
- Dynamic Type: the label uses `.ds(.button)` and scales, but the track is a fixed 56pt tall, so long labels at large sizes will clip.

## See also

- [DSButton](DSButton.md)
- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSToggle.md -->

# DSToggle

A themed on/off switch whose knob springs across a pill track and snaps with a rigid haptic.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSToggle.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSToggle.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ToggleDemo: View {
    @State private var notifications = true
    @State private var compact = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                DSToggle("Push notifications", isOn: $notifications)
                DSToggle("Compact layout", isOn: $compact, size: .small)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `String?` | `nil` | Text shown beside the switch (unlabeled first argument). |
| `isOn` | `Binding<Bool>` | required | The on/off state. |
| `size` | `DSToggleSize` | `.medium` | `.small` (42x26) or `.medium` (51x31). |
| `onColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Track color when on. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.rigid` | Haptic fired on change. |



## Variants

- `.medium` matches the native switch size; `.small` suits dense settings lists.
- Without a label it is just the switch, for use in your own rows:

```swift
DSToggle(isOn: $notifications).accessibilityLabel("Push notifications")
```
- `.disabled(true)` dims it to 50% and suppresses the haptic.

## Behavior

- The knob springs across the track with `DSAnimation.springSnappy`. The track fills with `onColor` (theme accent by default) when on and with the palette border color when off.
- A rigid haptic fires on every change (not when disabled).

## Accessibility

- One accessibility element. Its label is the `label` text; when you use the toggle without a label, add `.accessibilityLabel("…")` yourself.
- Value is "On" or "Off", with the toggle trait, and it reads as dimmed when `.disabled`.
- Dynamic Type: the optional label text scales with the user's text size.

## See also

- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [DSStepper](DSStepper.md)
- [DSButton](DSButton.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSRadioGroup.md -->

# DSRadioGroup

A single-select list for any `Hashable` value: the indicator pops to the accent while its dot grows, and a frosted highlight slides to the chosen row.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSRadioGroup.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSRadioGroup.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct RadioGroupDemo: View {
    enum Plan: Hashable { case free, pro, team }

    @State private var plan = Plan.pro
    @State private var shipping = "Standard"

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSCard {
                    DSRadioGroup(selection: $plan, options: [
                        DSRadioOption("Free", value: Plan.free, subtitle: "For trying things out"),
                        DSRadioOption("Pro", value: Plan.pro, subtitle: "Everything, for one person"),
                        DSRadioOption("Team", value: Plan.team, subtitle: "Shared workspaces"),
                    ])
                    .accessibilityLabel("Plan")
                }

                DSCard {
                    DSRadioGroup(selection: $shipping, options: ["Standard", "Express", "Overnight"])
                        .accessibilityLabel("Shipping speed")
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

`DSRadioGroup(selection:options:accent:haptic:)`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `selection` | `Binding<Value>` | required | The chosen value (`Value: Hashable`). |
| `options` | `[DSRadioOption<Value>]` | required | The rows, top to bottom. Values must be unique. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill of the selected indicator. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.rigid` | Haptic fired when the selection changes. |

Build each option with `DSRadioOption(_ title: String, value: Value, subtitle: String? = nil, icon: String? = nil)`.

**String shortcut:** `DSRadioGroup(selection: Binding<String>, options: [String], accent: Color? = nil, haptic: DSHapticStyle = .rigid)`, available when `Value` is `String`; each string is both the label and the value.

## Variants

```swift
DSRadioGroup(
    selection: $payment,
    options: [
        DSRadioOption("Apple Pay", value: 1, icon: "apple.logo"),
        DSRadioOption("Credit card", value: 2, subtitle: "Visa ending 4242", icon: "creditcard"),
    ],
    accent: theme.palette.success
)
```
Here `payment` is an `Int` state and `theme` is `@DSThemed private var theme`. Any `Hashable` works as the value: an enum, an id, an `Int`, a `UUID`.

## Behavior

- Tapping anywhere on a row selects it. Rows are at least 44 pt tall and as wide as the group. Wrap the group in a `DSCard` for the glass container look.
- The indicator is a 24 pt filled ring (two fills, no stroke; the outer disc is `palette.textSecondary`, at least 3:1 against the card in light and dark), the same size, colors and haptic as `DSCheckbox`. On select the accent layer springs up from 55 % size with `springBouncy` and fades in, and an inner dot grows a beat later. The previous row's indicator shrinks and fades.
- A highlight (`theme.subtleFill`) slides to the chosen row with `matchedGeometryEffect` and `springSmooth`, resizing between rows with and without a subtitle. Nothing else changes size, so the list never jumps.
- Everything follows `selection`, so changing it from outside (a "reset" button) animates like a tap.
- The haptic fires on a change only: reselecting the current value does nothing. A disabled group dims to 50 % and ignores taps.
- The dot is `theme.onAccent` on the accent fill, and `palette.textOnPrimary` when you pass your own `accent`.
- Reduce Motion: nothing pops, grows or slides. The indicators and the highlight crossfade in place.
- Press: the row dips with `DSPress.scale`.

## Accessibility

- Each row is one button. Its label is the title followed by the subtitle, its value is its position ("2 of 3"), and it carries the selected trait while chosen. Choosing a row also announces "Title, selected".
- The group is a container. Label it for VoiceOver with `.accessibilityLabel("Plan")`.
- Dynamic Type: titles and subtitles scale with the user's text size and rows grow to fit.

## See also

- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [DSListCell](DSListCell.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSStepper.md -->

# DSStepper

A minus / number / plus stepper on a glass track. The number rolls, and hitting a limit wiggles the track with a warning haptic so you feel the refusal.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSStepper.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSStepper.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct StepperDemo: View {
    @State private var guests = 2

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            HStack {
                Text("Guests").ds(.title3)
                Spacer()
                DSStepper(value: $guests, in: 1...8)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Guests")
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `Binding<Int>` | required | The current number. |
| `range` | `ClosedRange<Int>` | `0...99` | Allowed values. Declared as `in range:` at the call site. |
| `step` | `Int` | `1` | Amount added or removed per tap. A non-positive step is treated as 1. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Tint of the − and + glyphs. Defaults to theme ink (the number itself always uses the primary text color). |

Stepping clamps into `range`, so a `step` that doesn't divide the range evenly lands on the bound instead of overshooting. If the bound value starts outside `range`, the next step snaps it to the nearest bound.

## Variants

```swift
DSStepper(value: $quantity, in: 0...10, step: 2)
```
At a bound the buttons dim but stay tappable on purpose, so the refusal can be felt.

## Behavior

- The number rolls with a numeric text transition on each change.
- Each successful step fires a selection haptic.
- At a bound the value doesn't move; the track does a short jiggle with a warning haptic.
- Reduce Motion: the jiggle is skipped (the warning haptic still fires).
- Reduce Transparency: the glass track becomes a solid elevated background.

## Accessibility

- One adjustable element: "Stepper", value is the number. Swipe up or down to step.
- Override the label with `.accessibilityLabel("Guests")`, as in the snippet above.
- Dynamic Type: the control has a fixed 44pt height and the glyphs are fixed size. The number uses `.ds(.numeric)` and scales, but its width is reserved from the range, so keep ranges short.

## See also

- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [DSRating](DSRating.md)
- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSRating.md -->

# DSRating

A star rating you can drag or tap, with a selection tick per star and a pop on the active one. It also has a read-only form with fractional fills.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSRating.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSRating.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct RatingDemo: View {
    @State private var stars = 3.0

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("How was your stay?").ds(.title3)
                DSRating(rating: $stars, step: 0.5)
                DSRating(value: 4.5)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rating` | `Binding<Double>` | required | Current rating, in `0...count`. |
| `count` | `Int` | `5` | Number of stars (minimum 1). |
| `step` | `Double` | `1` | Snap increment: `1` for whole stars, `0.5` for half stars. |
| `symbol` | `String` | `"star.fill"` | SF Symbol for a filled star. |
| `emptySymbol` | `String` | `"star"` | SF Symbol for an empty star. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `28` | Point size of each star. |
| `spacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xs` | Gap between stars. |
| `tint` | `Color?` | `nil` | Rated star color. Defaults to the warning amber. |
| `emptyColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Unrated star color. Defaults to the border color. |
| `haptics` | `Bool` | `true` | Fire haptics while rating. |

**Read-only init:** `DSRating(value: Double, count: Int = 5, symbol: String = "star.fill", emptySymbol: String = "star", size: CGFloat = 20, spacing: CGFloat = DSSpacing.xxs, tint: Color? = nil, emptyColor: Color? = nil)`. It fills stars fractionally (4.5 shows four and a half) and ignores touches.

## Variants

```swift
DSRating(rating: $stars, count: 10, symbol: "heart.fill", emptySymbol: "heart", tint: .pink)
```
Use `step: 0.5` for half stars. Use `DSRating(value:)` for displaying averages.

## Behavior

- Drag across the stars or tap one; the value snaps to `step` (`0.25` gives quarter stars). A rating bound outside `0...count` is drawn and read as the nearest bound.
- A selection tick fires each time the finger enters a new star, and a light haptic on release. The active star pops with a bouncy spring.
- Reduce Motion: no pop, and the fill eases quickly instead of springing.

## Accessibility

- Editable: one adjustable element labelled "Rating" with the value "3 out of 5 stars". Swipe up or down to move one `step`; an off-step value (say 2.3) moves onto the step grid, and swiping down from the first star clears the rating to 0.
- The read-only init has the same label and value format ("Rating", "3.5 out of 5 stars", up to two decimals: "4.33") and isn't adjustable.
- Dynamic Type: stars are sized by the `size` parameter, so they don't scale with text size.

## See also

- [DSStepper](DSStepper.md)
- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSSegmentedControl.md -->

# DSSegmentedControl

A generic segmented control where a filled pill (or an accent underline) slides between options, with a selection tick on each change.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSegmentedControl.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSegmentedControl.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SegmentedControlDemo: View {
    enum Range: Hashable { case day, week, month }

    @State private var range = Range.week
    @State private var tab = "Overview"

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSSegmentedControl(
                    selection: $range,
                    segments: [
                        DSSegment("Day", value: Range.day),
                        DSSegment("Week", value: Range.week),
                        DSSegment("Month", value: Range.month),
                    ]
                )
                DSSegmentedControl(
                    selection: $tab,
                    options: ["Overview", "Details", "Reviews"],
                    style: .underline
                )
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `selection` | `Binding<Value>` | required | The selected value (`Value: Hashable`). |
| `segments` | `[DSSegment<Value>]` | required | The options. Build each with `DSSegment(_ title: String, value: Value, icon: String? = nil)`. |
| `style` | `DSSegmentedControlStyle` | `.pill` | `.pill` or `.underline`. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | `.underline` only: overrides both the underline and the selected label. Without it the underline is the theme accent and the selected label is theme ink. Ignored by `.pill`. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.selection` | Haptic fired when the selection changes. |

**String shortcut:** `DSSegmentedControl(selection: Binding<String>, options: [String], style: DSSegmentedControlStyle = .pill, accent: Color? = nil, haptic: DSHapticStyle = .selection)`, available when `Value` is `String`.

## Variants

- `.pill`: a raised elevated-background indicator on a rounded secondary-background track, like the native iOS control.
- `.underline`: an accent underline beneath the labels, tab-bar style.
- Segments can carry an SF Symbol: `DSSegment("Map", value: Mode.map, icon: "map")`.

## Behavior

- The indicator slides between segments with a snappy spring (shared geometry).
- A selection haptic fires on each change; tapping the already-selected segment does nothing.

## Accessibility

- Each segment is a separate button labelled with its title, and marked selected when active. An icon is hidden from VoiceOver when the segment has a title.
- Label text doesn't scale with Dynamic Type yet: the control has a fixed height, so its label keeps a fixed size. Text elsewhere on your screen that uses `.ds(_:)` / `.dsTextStyle(_:)` does scale.

## See also

- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [DSPageControl](DSPageControl.md)
- [DSStepper](DSStepper.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSTextField.md -->

# DSTextField

A labelled text input with leading icon, secure mode and validation states, plus a matching `DSSearchBar` with a clear button.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSTextField.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSTextField.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct TextFieldDemo: View {
    @State private var email = ""
    @State private var password = ""
    @State private var query = ""

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                DSSearchBar(placeholder: "Search destinations", text: $query)
                DSTextField(
                    label: "Email",
                    placeholder: "you@example.com",
                    icon: "envelope",
                    text: $email,
                    state: email.isEmpty || email.contains("@") ? .normal : .error("Enter a valid email")
                )
                DSTextField(
                    label: "Password",
                    placeholder: "At least 8 characters",
                    icon: "lock",
                    text: $password,
                    isSecure: true
                )
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `String` | `""` | Caption above the field; hidden when empty. |
| `placeholder` | `String` | required | Placeholder text. |
| `icon` | `String?` | `nil` | Leading SF Symbol. |
| `text` | `Binding<String>` | required | The field's text. |
| `state` | `DSTextFieldState` | `.normal` | `.normal`, `.focused`, `.error(String)`, `.success` or `.disabled`. |
| `isSecure` | `Bool` | `false` | Use a secure (password) field. |

**DSSearchBar:** `DSSearchBar(placeholder: String = "Search", text: Binding<String>)`. A pill-shaped search field with a magnifier and a clear button that appears once there is text.

## Variants

- `.normal`: neutral. Real keyboard focus tints the icon and a 1.5pt outline with theme ink. `.focused` is accepted but looks the same as `.normal`; focus is read from the system, not from `state`.
- `.error("message")`: red outline, a red warning icon and the message below the field.
- `.success`: a green check mark appears (the green outline shows only while focused).
- `.disabled`: dimmed to 50%.

## Behavior

- Focusing a field tints it with the theme ink; validation states change color and icon.
- The search bar's clear button fires a light haptic.

## Accessibility

- The field is a standard SwiftUI `TextField` (or `SecureField`); VoiceOver uses its placeholder as the field name, and `label` is shown as visible text above it.
- Override the spoken name with `.accessibilityLabel("Email address")`.
- Dynamic Type: the caption above the field and the error message use `.ds(_:)` and scale. The typed text and placeholder use a fixed-size font inside a fixed-height box (48pt; `DSSearchBar` is 44pt), so they do not.

## See also

- [DSCodeField](DSCodeField.md)
- [DSButton](DSButton.md)
- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSCodeField.md -->

# DSCodeField

A one-time-code input of separate digit boxes with a blinking caret, a springy active box, and a shake on a wrong code.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSCodeField.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSCodeField.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct CodeFieldDemo: View {
    @State private var code = ""
    @State private var state = DSCodeFieldState.normal

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("Enter the 6-digit code we texted you").ds(.callout)
                DSCodeField(code: $code, state: state) { entered in
                    state = (entered == "123456") ? .success : .error
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `length` | `Int` | `6` | Number of digit boxes. |
| `code` | `Binding<String>` | required | The digits entered so far. Digits only, clamped to `length`. |
| `state` | `DSCodeFieldState` | `.normal` | `.normal`, `.error` or `.success`. |
| `boxHeight` | `CGFloat` | `56` | Height of each box. |
| `onComplete` | `((String) -> Void)?` | `nil` | Called with the full code once `length` digits are entered. |



## Variants

- `.normal`: neutral boxes.
- `.error`: red boxes, a shake and an error haptic. Clear `code` and reset `state` to retry.
- `.success`: green boxes and a success haptic.

## Behavior

- Tap anywhere on the field to focus a hidden text field that owns the keyboard (number pad on iOS).
- On iOS the field supports SMS one-time-code autofill.
- The active box scales up with a snappy spring, a caret blinks in it, and each digit fires a light haptic.

## Accessibility

- One element labelled "Verification code" that accepts typing.
- Its value spells the digits and progress, for example "1 2 3, 3 of 6 digits", plus ", incorrect code" for `.error` or ", verified" for `.success`.
- Dynamic Type: the digits use `.ds(.title1)` and scale, but each box keeps the fixed `boxHeight`, so very large sizes can clip.

## See also

- [DSTextField](DSTextField.md)
- [DSButton](DSButton.md)
- [DSSlideToConfirm](DSSlideToConfirm.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)
