<!-- source: docs/components/DSSkeleton.md -->

# DSSkeleton

Loading placeholders: a shimmering block you compose by hand, and a `.dsSkeleton(_:)` modifier that turns a real view into its own placeholder so the loading layout can't drift from the loaded one.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSkeleton.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSkeleton.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SkeletonDemo: View {
    @State private var isLoading = true

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                // Hand-built placeholder
                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    DSSkeleton.circle(DSSpacing.huge)
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                        DSSkeleton(width: 140)
                        DSSkeleton(width: 90)
                    }
                }

                // The real view, shown as its own placeholder while loading
                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    DSAvatar(name: "Ada Lovelace", size: DSSpacing.huge)
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xxs) {
                        Text("Ada Lovelace").ds(.title3)
                        Text("Analyst, mathematician").ds(.callout)
                    }
                }
                .dsSkeleton(isLoading)

                DSToggle("Loading", isOn: $isLoading)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

`DSSkeleton(width:height:cornerRadius:)`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `width` | `CGFloat?` | `nil` | Fixed width. `nil` fills the available width. |
| `height` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.sm` | Block height. |
| `cornerRadius` | `CGFloat` | `DSRadius.xs` | Corner radius. |

`DSSkeleton.circle(_ diameter:)` makes a round block, e.g. for an avatar.

`View.dsSkeleton(_ isLoading: Bool)` takes only the loading flag.

## Variants

```swift
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
    DSSkeleton(height: 160, cornerRadius: DSRadius.surface)
    DSSkeleton(height: DSSpacing.md)
    DSSkeleton(width: 120)
}
```
A feed-style block: image, title line, short subtitle.

## Behavior

- `DSSkeleton` is a block in the wash colour (on a backdrop) or the palette border colour (elsewhere), with a shimmer sweep.
- `.dsSkeleton(true)` redacts the view as placeholder shapes of its own layout, pulses its opacity gently between full and half (a 3.6 s cycle sampled from a timeline, so it stops the moment loading ends), and blocks touches.
- When `isLoading` goes false the redaction lifts with a short fade.
- The wrapped view keeps its identity when the flag flips: its `@State`, `.task` and `.onAppear` are not reset or run twice. That is why the modifier pulses instead of sweeping: a sweep needs a second copy of the content.
- Reduce Motion: no shimmer and no pulse. Placeholders rest at full opacity.

## Accessibility

- `DSSkeleton` blocks are hidden from VoiceOver.
- While `.dsSkeleton(true)` is active the view reads as one element labelled "Loading". When it ends, the real content is announced normally.

## See also

- [DSEmptyState](DSEmptyState.md)
- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSSuccessCheck.md -->

# DSSuccessCheck

An animated success seal: the ring strokes itself, the disc fills, the checkmark draws, and the whole thing pops once with a soft halo and a success haptic on the same beat.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSuccessCheck.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSuccessCheck.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SuccessCheckDemo: View {
    @State private var isPaid = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSSuccessCheck(isComplete: isPaid, size: 96, accessibilityLabel: "Payment sent")
                    .padding(DSSpacing.md)
                Text(isPaid ? "Payment sent" : "Ready to pay").ds(.title2)
                DSButton(isPaid ? "Reset" : "Pay $24.00", isFullWidth: true) {
                    isPaid.toggle()
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isComplete` | `Bool` | required | Plays the animation when it becomes `true`. Fades the seal out when `false`. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `64` | Diameter of the seal. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Ring and disc fill. Defaults to the theme's success color. The checkmark uses the palette's text-on-primary color. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `.success` | Fired as the check completes. `nil` for none. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `String` | `"Done"` | What VoiceOver says, and announces when the seal completes. |

## Variants

```swift
HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
    DSSuccessCheck(isComplete: true, size: 32)
    DSSuccessCheck(isComplete: true, size: 48, color: DSColors.info, haptic: nil)
}
```
The seal is only a fill and two strokes, so it works at any size from a list row up to a hero.

## Behavior

- The animation plays when `isComplete` becomes `true`, and once on first appear if it already is. A view that re-appears already complete (tab switch, navigating back) shows the finished seal at rest, with no haptic or announcement. It takes about 0.9 seconds.
- Order: the ring strokes itself, the disc fills behind it, then the check draws. A single spring pop peaks as the check finishes, together with one soft halo that expands and fades.
- The haptic fires at that peak, not at the start.
- When `isComplete` goes back to `false` the seal fades out quietly. Setting it to `true` again replays the animation.
- The halo extends past `size`; leave a little room around the seal.
- Reduce Motion: no strokes and no pop. The finished seal crossfades in, and the haptic still fires.

## Accessibility

- While complete, the seal is one image element labelled with your `accessibilityLabel`. While not complete it is hidden from VoiceOver.
- When it completes, the label is announced.
- Give it a label that says what happened ("Payment sent") rather than the default.

## See also

- [Progress](Progress.md) for work that is still running
- [Motion](Motion.md) for ambient effects
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSTypewriterText.md -->

# DSTypewriterText

Text that types a phrase out character by character, holds it, erases it and moves on to the next, with a blinking caret. For hero headlines and empty states that need a little life.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSTypewriterText.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSTypewriterText.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct TypewriterDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("Build something").ds(.largeTitle)
                DSTypewriterText(
                    ["that feels alive.", "with glass and springs.", "in an afternoon."],
                    style: .title1
                )

                DSTypewriterText(["Ready when you are."], style: .callout, loops: false)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

Keep phrases short enough to fit on one line: the view is single line and reserves the width of the widest phrase.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ phrases` | `[String]` | required | Phrases to cycle through, in order. An empty array renders nothing. |
| `style` | `DSTextStyle` | `.title1` | Text style for the phrases. |
| `typingSpeed` | `TimeInterval` | `0.06` | Seconds per character while typing. |
| `erasingSpeed` | `TimeInterval` | `0.03` | Seconds per character while erasing. Should be faster than typing. |
| `holdDuration` | `TimeInterval` | `1.4` | Seconds a fully typed phrase stays before erasing. |
| `loops` | `Bool` | `true` | When `false`, stops on the last phrase fully typed (the caret keeps blinking). |
| `caretColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Caret fill. Defaults to the theme accent. |

## Variants

- **Rotating headline**: several phrases with `loops: true`.
- **Type once**: `loops: false` types the last phrase and stays (the snippet's second view).
- **Speed**: raise `typingSpeed` for a calmer feel; the defaults are about 16 characters per second.

## Behavior

- Steps through grapheme clusters, so emoji and accented characters are never split.
- Driven by a cancellable `Task`: cancelled on disappear and restarted when `phrases` or Reduce Motion changes.
- The caret blinks in `caretColor`; it is a thin capsule sized to the text style.
- No haptics.
- Reduce Motion: no typing or erasing; the full phrase is shown, still cycling through the list, and the caret stays solid.

## Accessibility

- The view is one element labelled with the whole current phrase, so VoiceOver never reads a half-typed fragment. The caret is decorative.
- Because the label changes when the phrase changes, avoid putting it where VoiceOver users need stable text, such as the only copy of an instruction.
- The text style applied through `.ds(_:)` scales with Dynamic Type. Check that your widest phrase still fits on one line at large sizes.

## See also

- [DSThinkingIndicator](DSThinkingIndicator.md)
- [DSEmptyState](DSEmptyState.md)
- [Motion](Motion.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/Motion.md -->

# Motion

Five composable view modifiers for ambient motion: breathe, jiggle, pop in, edge sweep and hue drift. Springs for touch, eased curves for ambience, and every one has a real Reduce Motion state.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSMotion.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Animation/DSMotion.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct MotionDemo: View {
    @State private var shakes = 0
    @State private var isSweeping = true

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                Circle()
                    .fill(Color.green)
                    .frame(width: 16, height: 16)
                    .dsBreathe(.subtle)

                Image(systemName: "bell.fill")
                    .font(.largeTitle)
                    .dsJiggle(trigger: shakes)
                DSButton("Shake", variant: .secondary, size: .small) { shakes += 1 }

                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { index in
                        RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: DSRadius.control, style: .continuous)
                            .fill(Color.blue)
                            .frame(height: DSSpacing.huge)
                            .dsHueDrift()
                            .dsPopIn(delay: Double(index) * 0.08)
                    }
                }

                Text("Processing…")
                    .ds(.body)
                    .padding(DSSpacing.md)
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
                    .dsSurface(.glass, radius: DSRadius.card)
                    .dsEdgeSweep(radius: DSRadius.card, isActive: isSweeping)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

### `.dsBreathe(_:)`

`func dsBreathe(_ intensity: DSBreatheIntensity = .medium) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ intensity` | `DSBreatheIntensity` | `.medium` | How far it swells: `.subtle` (1.02), `.medium` (1.05), `.strong` (1.10). |

### `.dsJiggle(trigger:)`

`func dsJiggle<T: Equatable>(trigger: T) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `T: Equatable` | required | One decaying wiggle fires every time this value changes. |

### `.dsPopIn(delay:)`

`func dsPopIn(delay: Double = 0) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delay` | `Double` | `0` | Seconds before the entrance starts. Stagger by index: `Double(index) * 0.08`. |

### `.dsEdgeSweep(radius:isActive:)`

`func dsEdgeSweep(radius: CGFloat = DSRadius.card, isActive: Bool = true) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `CGFloat` | `DSRadius.card` | Corner radius of the surface underneath. Match it. |
| `isActive` | `Bool` | `true` | Fades the highlight in and out. |

### `.dsHueDrift(isActive:)`

`func dsHueDrift(isActive: Bool = true) -> some View`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isActive` | `Bool` | `true` | Turns the drift on or off. |

### `DSMotion.loop(_:autoreverses:unless:)`

For your own ambient effects: `DSMotion.loop(_ base: Animation, autoreverses: Bool = true, unless reduceMotion: Bool) -> Animation?` wraps an animation in `repeatForever`, or returns `nil` under Reduce Motion, so the change applies instantly and the effect rests instead of being skipped.

## Variants

| Modifier | Use it for | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| `.dsBreathe` | "alive and waiting": loading states, status dots, avatars | 2.4s ease-in-out loop, scale plus a slight opacity dip |
| `.dsJiggle` | a rejected input, an item that needs noticing | 0.45s, peak 7 degrees, decaying counter-swings |
| `.dsPopIn` | entrances and staggered rows | `springBouncy` overshoot from 0.8 scale |
| `.dsEdgeSweep` | processing, recording, "AI is working" | 2.0s linear loop of a specular highlight on the 1pt glass edge |
| `.dsHueDrift` | decorative life on a solid fill | 8.0s loop, at most 12 degrees of hue rotation |

The constants live on `DSMotion` (`breatheDuration`, `sweepDuration`, `driftDuration`, `driftDegrees`, `jiggleDegrees`, `jiggleDuration`).

`.dsPulse()` is deprecated; use `.dsBreathe(_:)` instead.

## Behavior

- All five settle at a resting state under Reduce Motion instead of being skipped: breathe and drift stop looping, the jiggle does not rotate, the edge sweep shows its highlight without travelling, and pop in keeps the fade but drops the scale.
- Colors come from the theme (the edge sweep is light riding the existing glass edge, not a border).
- The loops are ambient, so they do not fire haptics; add a `DSHapticEngine.shared.fire(.error)` next to a jiggle if the event deserves one.

## Accessibility

- These modifiers are purely visual and do not change what VoiceOver reads.
- Because Reduce Motion is a real state, content stays visible and in place when the setting is on.
- Never use motion as the only signal: pair a jiggle with an error message, and a sweep with a status text such as "Processing…".

## See also

- [dsScrollReveal](DSScrollReveal.md) (scroll-coupled reveal)
- [DSThinkingIndicator](DSThinkingIndicator.md)
- [Progress](Progress.md)
- [DSAvatar](DSAvatar.md) (breathe while waiting)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSConfetti.md -->

# dsConfetti

A one-shot burst of confetti from any point of a view, fired whenever a trigger value changes. Colored from the active theme.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSConfetti.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Animation/DSConfetti.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ConfettiDemo: View {
    @State private var celebrations = 0

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                Text("Order placed").ds(.title2)
                DSButton("Celebrate") { celebrations += 1 }
            }
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
            .dsConfetti(trigger: celebrations, origin: UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0.6))
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | `Equatable` | required | One burst fires every time this value changes. It does not fire on first appearance. |
| `origin` | `UnitPoint` | `.center` | Where the burst starts, in the unit space of the view you attach it to. |
| `count` | `Int` | `80` | Number of pieces, limited to 150. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `nil` | Haptic fired with the burst. |

## Variants

```swift
struct ConfettiCornersDemo: View {
    @State private var left = 0
    @State private var right = 0

    var body: some View {
        VStack {
            DSButton("Both corners") { left += 1; right += 1 }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity)
        .dsConfetti(trigger: left, origin: .bottomLeading, count: 50)
        .dsConfetti(trigger: right, origin: .bottomTrailing, count: 50, haptic: .success)
    }
}
```

Attach it to a container that covers the area the paper should fall through, such as the screen root, and pick `origin` in that container's unit space. Pieces are drawn inside the bounds of the view the modifier is attached to.

## Behavior

- Pieces fan upward and outward, slow down from air drag, then drift down under gravity while spinning and tumbling.
- Each piece lives 1.6 to 2.4 s and fades out over the last 30%.
- Colors come from the theme: the accent, the theme ink, a lighter tint of each, and the ink again for weight, which keeps the burst visible against every page tone.
- Several triggers in a row overlap; earlier pieces finish their fall.
- Nothing runs while idle: the animation stops once the last piece is gone.
- `haptic` is `nil` by default because the action that triggers confetti (a button press, a confirmed slide) usually has its own haptic. Set it when the trigger is a state change with no haptic of its own.
- Reduce Motion: no pieces are drawn. The haptic, if set, still fires.

## Accessibility

- Purely decorative: ignores touches and is hidden from VoiceOver.
- Announce the outcome in your own UI (the success text or a toast), not through the confetti.

## See also

- [DSSlideToConfirm](DSSlideToConfirm.md)
- [DSToast](DSToast.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSScrollReveal.md -->

# dsScrollReveal

A scroll-coupled reveal for any repeated view: it sits at full presence inside the scroll view, recedes (a little smaller, a little dimmer) as it crosses the leading or trailing edge, and comes back when you scroll back.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSScrollEffects.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Animation/DSScrollEffects.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

Put `.dsScrollReveal(_:)` on each repeated item, inside the `ScrollView`:

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ScrollRevealDemo: View {
    private let items = ["Weekly summary", "New follower", "Backup complete", "Battery full", "Trip reminder", "Goal reached"]

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                ForEach(items, id: \.self) { title in
                    DSCard {
                        Text(title)
                            .ds(.title3)
                            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                    }
                    .dsScrollReveal()
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

For a horizontal carousel, size each card with `containerRelativeFrame`, leave margins with `contentMargins` so the neighbours peek, and use `.strong`:

```swift
ScrollView(.horizontal) {
    HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
        ForEach(0..<5, id: \.self) { index in
            DSCard { Text("Card \(index + 1)").ds(.title3) }
                .containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal)
                .dsScrollReveal(.strong)
        }
    }
    .scrollTargetLayout()
}
.contentMargins(.horizontal, DSSpacing.xxxl, for: .scrollContent)
.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
```

## Parameters

`func dsScrollReveal(_ intensity: DSScrollRevealIntensity = .medium) -> some View`

| Intensity | Scale at the edge | Opacity at the edge | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.subtle` | `DSMotion.scrollRevealSubtleScale` (0.96) | `scrollRevealSubtleOpacity` (0.65) | Text rows and list cells. |
| `.medium` (default) | `scrollRevealMediumScale` (0.90) | `scrollRevealMediumOpacity` (0.40) | Cards in a feed. |
| `.strong` | `scrollRevealStrongScale` (0.80) | `scrollRevealStrongOpacity` (0.15) | Carousel cards. |

## Behavior

- Built on `scrollTransition(.interactive)`: the amount follows the scroll position continuously, in both directions, so it is not an entrance that fires once (that is `dsPopIn` / `dsStaggerIn`).
- It reacts at the edges of the scroll view's visible area, not at its centre. A row fully inside is at full presence; in a carousel with peeking neighbours that reads as centre emphasis. If several cards are fully visible at once, they all stay at full presence.
- The axis is inferred from the enclosing scroll view. Only scale and opacity change (render transforms), so nothing reflows and neighbours never shift.
- Ambient, so it fires no haptic.

## Accessibility

- Under Reduce Motion every item rests at full presence: no scaling and no dimming, so contrast is never reduced for the people the setting protects.
- It does not change what VoiceOver reads or the order of the elements.

## See also

- [Motion](Motion.md) for the other ambient modifiers
- [DSCarousel](DSCarousel.md) for a ready-made snapping carousel with its own depth effect
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSMarquee.md -->

# DSMarquee

Content that scrolls horizontally in a seamless loop — but only when it is too wide to fit. A "now playing" line, a long title, a ticker of stats: text that would otherwise truncate keeps moving so all of it can be read. Content that already fits stays put.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSMarquee.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSMarquee.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct NowPlaying: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                Text("Now playing").ds(.overline, color: DSColors.textSecondary)

                DSMarquee {
                    Text("Midnight City · M83 · Hurry Up, We're Dreaming").ds(.callout)
                }

                // Any content, not just text — it scrolls as one line.
                DSMarquee(velocity: 28) {
                    HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                        DSBadge("LIVE", variant: .filled)
                        Text("Breaking news scrolls by, in full").ds(.footnote)
                    }
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

Keep the content to a single line (text, a badge, a small row). The marquee measures that line and scrolls it only when it is wider than the space it has.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `velocity` | `CGFloat` | `40` | Scroll speed in points per second. Linear, so the pace reads constant for any length. `0` disables scrolling. |
| `spacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxxl` (40) | Gap between the end of one copy and the start of the next in the loop. |
| `fade` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.lg` (20) | Width of the soft edge fade on each side. Pass `0` for hard edges. |
| `content` | `() -> Content` | required | The content to scroll, as a trailing `@ViewBuilder` closure. |

## Behavior

- **Scrolls only on overflow.** If the content fits the available width it is shown static and left-aligned, with no motion and no fade.
- **Seamless loop.** The offset is sampled from a `TimelineView(.animation)`, which only ticks while the marquee is on screen, so an off-screen or scrolled-away marquee costs nothing. Two copies of the content are laid end to end with `spacing` between them, translated left by exactly one copy's width plus the gap, then wrapped — so the join never shows.
- **Edge fades.** A gradient mask (not a border) softens both edges while scrolling, hinting that the line continues past them. A static overflow fades only the trailing edge.
- **No haptics.** The marquee is ambient, not interactive.
- **Reduce Motion:** no scrolling. The content is shown static from its start with a trailing fade, so it is clearly truncated rather than frozen mid-scroll.

## Accessibility

- The content is exposed as a single combined element, so VoiceOver reads the whole line at once regardless of where the scroll happens to be. The second, looping copy and the hidden measuring copy are excluded from accessibility.
- Text styled with `.ds(_:)` scales with Dynamic Type; the line simply grows wider and scrolls further.
- Prefer a marquee for supplementary, glanceable copy (a track title, a status line). Don't put text a user must act on only inside a moving line.

## See also

- [DSTypewriterText](DSTypewriterText.md)
- [DSNumberTicker](DSNumberTicker.md)
- [Motion](Motion.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSChip.md -->

# DSChip / DSChipGroup

Selectable pill chips for filters, tags, categories and interest pickers. `DSChipGroup` lays them out with [`DSFlowLayout`](DSFlowLayout.md), which breaks onto as many lines as the width needs, and manages single or multiple selection. Selecting a chip springs its fill into the accent and ticks a selection haptic.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSChip.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSChip.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ChipDemo: View {
    @State private var topics: Set<String> = ["Design"]
    @State private var sort: String? = "Trending"

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                // Multiple selection — tap to add or remove.
                DSChipGroup(
                    ["Design", "Engineering", "Product", "Research", "Marketing"],
                    selection: $topics
                )
                // Single selection — tap the selected chip again to clear it.
                DSChipGroup(["Trending", "Newest", "Top rated", "Nearby"], selection: $sort)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

### DSChipGroup

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `[DSChipItem<Value>]` | required | The chips, in order. Build each with `DSChipItem(_ title: String, value: Value, icon: String? = nil)` (`Value: Hashable`). |
| `selection` | `Binding<Set<Value>>` | required | Multiple selection: tapping a chip inserts or removes its value. |
| `selection` | `Binding<Value?>` | required | Single selection: tapping a chip selects it; tapping the selected chip clears it (`nil`). |
| `spacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xs` | Gap between chips and between lines. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill for selected chips. Defaults to the theme accent. |

**String shortcut:** `DSChipGroup(_ options: [String], selection: Binding<Set<String>>, …)` and `DSChipGroup(_ options: [String], selection: Binding<String?>, …)`, available when `Value` is `String` — each option is its own value.

### DSChip

A single chip you can place on its own (a filter outside a group, an "Add tag" affordance):

```swift
DSChip("Add tag", icon: "plus") { addTag() }
DSChip("Design", isSelected: isOn) { isOn.toggle() }
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `String` | required | The chip's label, and its VoiceOver label. |
| `icon` | `String?` | `nil` | Optional leading SF Symbol. Decorative — hidden from VoiceOver. |
| `isSelected` | `Bool` | `false` | Whether the chip reads as selected. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill when selected. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.selection` | Fired on tap. |
| `action` | `() -> Void` | required | Called on tap. In a `DSChipGroup` this toggles selection. |

## Variants

```swift
enum Sort: Hashable { case trending, newest, topRated }

struct ChipVariantsDemo: View {
    @State private var media: Set<String> = ["photos"]
    @State private var sort: Sort? = .trending
    @DSThemed private var theme

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
            // Leading icons and a custom accent for the selected fill
            DSChipGroup(
                [
                    DSChipItem("Photos", value: "photos", icon: "photo"),
                    DSChipItem("Videos", value: "videos", icon: "video"),
                    DSChipItem("Audio", value: "audio", icon: "waveform")
                ],
                selection: $media,
                accent: theme.palette.success
            )

            // Any Hashable value, not just strings
            DSChipGroup(
                [
                    DSChipItem("Trending", value: Sort.trending),
                    DSChipItem("Newest", value: Sort.newest),
                    DSChipItem("Top rated", value: Sort.topRated)
                ],
                selection: $sort,
                spacing: DSSpacing.sm
            )
        }
    }
}
```

## Behavior

- Chips flow left to right and wrap onto a new line whenever the next one would overflow the available width, using [`DSFlowLayout`](DSFlowLayout.md) — no horizontal scrolling. `DSChipGroup` depends on it, so copying `DSChip` into an app with the CLI brings it along.
- Selecting a chip crossfades its fill from `theme.subtleFill` to the accent with a snappy spring, lifts it with a soft shadow, and ticks a selection haptic.
- Pressing scales the chip to `DSPress.scale`. The press is a `ButtonStyle`, so a touch that becomes a scroll releases the chip instead of leaving it shrunk.
- No borders: an unselected chip reads through the subtle surface, a selected one through the accent fill.
- Reduce Motion: the fill changes with a quick fade instead of a spring.

## Accessibility

- Each chip is a button labelled with its title, and marked selected when active. A leading icon is decorative and hidden from VoiceOver.
- Chip labels use the `buttonSmall` text style, so they scale with Dynamic Type alongside the rest of your screen.
- A chip is as tall as its label plus `DSSpacing.xs` above and below, a little under the 44 pt minimum target. Keep `spacing` generous (`DSSpacing.sm`) where chips sit close together.

## See also

- [DSFlowLayout](DSFlowLayout.md)
- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [DSBadge](DSBadge.md)
- [DSButton](DSButton.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSFlowLayout.md -->

# DSFlowLayout

A wrapping layout: it lays its subviews out left-to-right and drops to a new line the moment the next one won't fit. The missing primitive behind tag clouds, filter chips, keyword lists and any set of pill-shaped items whose count you don't control — the one case a `VStack`/`HStack` can't handle and `DSGrid` gets wrong (chips aren't a grid; they're different widths).

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSFlowLayout.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Layout/DSFlowLayout.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct InterestsPicker: View {
    private let interests = ["Design", "SwiftUI", "Motion", "Accessibility",
                             "Haptics", "Typography", "Color", "Prototyping"]
    @State private var selected: Set<String> = ["SwiftUI", "Motion"]
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    @DSThemed private var theme

    var body: some View {
        DSFlowLayout {
            ForEach(interests, id: \.self) { interest in
                let isSelected = selected.contains(interest)
                Button {
                    dsHaptic(.selection)
                    withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : DSAnimation.springSnappy) {
                        selected.formSymmetricDifference([interest])
                    }
                } label: {
                    Text(interest)
                        .ds(.buttonSmall, color: isSelected ? theme.onAccent : theme.ink)
                        .padding(.horizontal, DSSpacing.sm)
                        .padding(.vertical, DSSpacing.xs)
                        .background(isSelected ? theme.accent : theme.subtleFill, in: Capsule())
                }
                .buttonStyle(.plain)
                .accessibilityAddTraits(isSelected ? .isSelected : [])
            }
        }
    }
}
```

`DSFlowLayout` is a `Layout`, not a container view: you use it exactly like a `VStack`, and it works with `ForEach`, conditional subviews and `withAnimation`. For ready-made selectable pills, see the chips in the Gallery's Flow Layout screen; the layout itself never draws anything.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xs` | Horizontal gap between items on the same row. |
| `lineSpacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xs` | Vertical gap between rows. |
| `alignment` | `HorizontalAlignment` | `.leading` | How a row narrower than the container sits within it: `.leading`, `.center` or `.trailing`. |

## Variants

```swift
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
    // Tighter rows, centred inside a card
    DSCard {
        DSFlowLayout(spacing: DSSpacing.xxs, lineSpacing: DSSpacing.xxs, alignment: .center) {
            ForEach(sizes, id: \.self) { size in
                DSBadge(size)
            }
        }
        .frame(maxWidth: .infinity)
    }

    // Right-aligned rows
    DSFlowLayout(alignment: .trailing) {
        ForEach(sizes, id: \.self) { size in
            DSBadge(size, variant: .soft)
        }
    }
}
```
`sizes` is any `[String]`. Alignment only has room to work when the layout is wider than its rows, which is why the centred example is stretched with `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)`.

## Behavior

- Greedy first-fit packing: items fill a row until the next one would overflow the proposed width, then wrap.
- It fills the width it is offered, so alignment has room to work. Offered no width (or an unbounded one, as in a horizontal `ScrollView`) it shrinks to its widest row.
- An item wider than the whole container gets a row to itself. It is measured again at the container width, so text wraps or truncates instead of running off the edge.
- Items shorter than their row sit vertically centred in it, like an `HStack`.
- Right-to-left languages mirror the layout: rows start on the right, and `.leading` / `.trailing` follow.
- Because it's a real `Layout`, motion is free and on-system: wrap a change to the content in `withAnimation(DSAnimation.springSmooth)` and items added, removed or resized glide to their new positions along the Velvet spring instead of snapping.
- Reports its true wrapped height, so it composes inside a `VStack`, a `DSCard` or a `ScrollView` with no fixed-height guesswork.

## Theming

A layout positions, it never paints — `DSFlowLayout` has no colors, fills or borders of its own and adds no haptics. Style the items you put inside it (a glass chip, a `DSBadge`, a `Button`) with the usual theme roles; selection feedback and haptics belong on those items, not on the layout.

## Accessibility

- Transparent to assistive tech: each subview keeps its own accessibility element, label, value and traits. VoiceOver reads the items in order. Mark a selected chip with `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isSelected)`.
- Dynamic Type: rows re-pack automatically as item widths grow with larger text, so nothing is clipped. Keep item labels on `.ds(_:)` so they scale.
- Reduce Motion: the layout has no motion of its own, and reflow animates only when you wrap the change in `withAnimation`. SwiftUI does not switch that off for you, so pass `nil` when `@Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion)` is on (the Usage snippet does) and items jump to their new places at rest.

## See also

- [DSBadge](DSBadge.md)
- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [Layout helpers](../components.md#layout) · [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSHoldToConfirm.md -->

# DSHoldToConfirm

A press-and-hold confirmation. A ring charges around a glass pill while you keep your finger down; when it closes the pill fills with the accent, runs your action and settles on a check. Let go early and it springs back without running anything.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSHoldToConfirm.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSHoldToConfirm.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct HoldToConfirmDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                Text("Delete account").ds(.title2)
                DSHoldToConfirm(
                    "Hold to delete",
                    icon: "trash",
                    confirmedLabel: "Deleted",
                    accent: DSColors.error
                ) {
                    try await deleteAccount()
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }

    // Stand-in for your call. Throwing re-opens the control for a retry.
    private func deleteAccount() async throws {
        try await Task.sleep(for: .seconds(1))
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `String` | required | Text on the pill (unlabeled first argument). |
| `icon` | `String?` | `nil` | SF Symbol before the label while idle. |
| `confirmedLabel` | `String` | `"Confirmed"` | Text shown once the action succeeds. |
| `duration` | `Double` | `1.2` | Seconds the finger must stay down. Anything under 0.2 is raised to 0.2. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Ring and fill color. Defaults to the theme accent; pass a status color for a destructive hold. |
| `isFullWidth` | `Bool` | `true` | Stretch to the available width. |
| `onConfirm` | `() async throws -> Void` | required | Runs once the ring closes. Throwing counts as a refusal. |

`onConfirm` works exactly as it does on [DSSlideToConfirm](DSSlideToConfirm.md): a plain synchronous closure also compiles, the control spins for at least half a second while it runs, and the closure carries the latency and the outcome.

## Variants

There is one look; what changes is how long you hold and what the accent says.

```swift
struct HoldToConfirmVariantsDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
            // A quick, compact hold.
            DSHoldToConfirm("Hold to send", icon: "paperplane.fill", confirmedLabel: "Sent", duration: 0.6, isFullWidth: false) { }
            // A slow, deliberate one.
            DSHoldToConfirm("Hold to power off", icon: "power", confirmedLabel: "Off", duration: 2.5) { }
        }
    }
}
```

Pick a hold when the risk is sustained intent (power off, hold-to-record) or when one hand is all the user has. Pick a slide when the risk is an accidental touch (a payment, a button a thumb could brush).

## Behavior

- Touch down: the pill dips (`DSPress.scale`), the ring starts to charge and a soft detent fires. Detents tick six times across the hold, each a little stronger.
- The action is decided by a timer that only completes if the finger stayed down, not by the ring animation, so a lift can never let a confirmation slip through.
- Ring closes: a pill-wide fill in the accent, a spinner while `onConfirm` runs, then a success haptic, a check and `confirmedLabel`.
- `onConfirm` throws: an error haptic, a short beat, then the ring clears and the control is ready for another try. It never words the failure; telling the user why is your job.
- Release early: a light haptic and the ring springs back. `onConfirm` is not called.
- There is no reset API. Re-mount with `.id(attempt)` to run it again.
- `.disabled(true)` dims it to 50% and ignores touches.
- Reduce Motion: the ring still charges, since it is the progress feedback itself, but the spring-back and the fill land with a plain fast ease instead of a bounce.
- Reduce Transparency: the glass pill becomes a solid elevated background.

## Accessibility

- One element, read as a button with the `label` you passed and the hint "Double-tap to confirm". VoiceOver users cannot hold a press, so a double-tap confirms straight away, with no timed hold.
- Value is "Processing" while `onConfirm` runs, then the `confirmedLabel` once done.
- Override the label with `.accessibilityLabel("Delete account")` on the outside.
- Dynamic Type: the label uses `.ds(.button)` and scales; the pill grows with it.

## See also

- [DSSlideToConfirm](DSSlideToConfirm.md)
- [DSButton](DSButton.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSSlider.md -->

# DSSlider

A continuous value slider on a slim track. An accent fill trails a white knob that lifts and glows under your finger; give it a `step` and it snaps to notches with a tick for each.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSSlider.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSSlider.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SliderDemo: View {
    @State private var volume = 0.6

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                HStack {
                    Text("Volume").ds(.title3)
                    Spacer()
                    Text("\(Int(volume * 100))%").ds(.numeric)
                }
                DSSlider(value: $volume)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Volume")
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

The slider draws no value of its own. Show a read-out beside it, as above, when people need to see the number.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `value` | `Binding<Double>` | required | The current value. It is kept inside `in`: an out-of-range value is clamped, and the clamped value is written back. |
| `bounds` | `ClosedRange<Double>` | `0...1` | Allowed values. Declared as `in bounds:` at the call site. Both ends must be finite. |
| `step` | `Double?` | `nil` | Snap increment, counted from the lower bound. `nil`, zero or negative means continuous. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill of the trail behind the knob. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `haptics` | `Bool` | `true` | Set `false` to silence the end detents and the notch ticks. |

Drag the knob, or tap anywhere on the track to jump there. The value is always clamped to `bounds`; with a `step` it is also snapped. The upper bound is always reachable: `0...10` by `3` has notches at 0, 3, 6, 9 and 10, the same way [DSStepper](DSStepper.md) lands on a bound it can't divide into.

## Variants

```swift
struct SliderVariantsDemo: View {
    @State private var price = 150.0
    @State private var temperature = -2.0
    @State private var opacity = 0.8

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
            // Notched: a selection tick on every 25.
            DSSlider(value: $price, in: 0...500, step: 25)
            // A range that crosses zero, in half-degree notches.
            DSSlider(value: $temperature, in: -10...10, step: 0.5)
            // Your own accent, and no haptics.
            DSSlider(value: $opacity, accent: DSColors.secondary, haptics: false)
            // Dimmed and inert.
            DSSlider(value: $opacity).disabled(true)
        }
    }
}
```

## Behavior

- The knob follows your finger on a light spring. Touching down on the track moves it to that spot.
- A continuous slider is silent while you drag and fires one rigid detent when you arrive at either end.
- A stepped slider also fires a selection tick each time the value lands on a new notch. Touching down on the notch it already rests on is silent.
- While grabbed, the knob lifts to 112% and a soft accent halo appears.
- Reduce Motion: the knob doesn't lift and follows your finger with no spring lag; the halo stays, since it is only a change of opacity.
- Disabled (`.disabled(true)`): dimmed to 50% and ignores touches.
- Reduce Transparency: nothing changes. The track is a flat fill, and the knob is opaque.
- On a `dsBackdrop()` screen the track is the frosted wash; on a plain screen it is the neutral grey [DSToggle](DSToggle.md) uses for its off track, so it never disappears into a white background.

## Accessibility

- One adjustable element: "Slider". Swipe up or down to change it: one notch for a stepped slider, a tenth of the range for a continuous one. Each move fires a selection tick.
- The value reads as "60 percent" for the default `0...1` continuous slider, and as the number itself otherwise ("150", "-2.5"), with as many decimals as `step` needs (two for a continuous slider).
- Override the label with `.accessibilityLabel("Volume")`, as in the snippet above. To change how the value is spoken (units, say), use `.accessibilityValue("150 dollars")`.
- A disabled slider ignores VoiceOver adjustments too.
- Dynamic Type: nothing in the control scales; the 44pt hit area is fixed.

## See also

- [DSStepper](DSStepper.md)
- [DSRating](DSRating.md)
- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSRangeSlider.md -->

# DSRangeSlider

Two knobs on one slim track, for picking a span: a price filter, an age range, opening hours. The accent fill runs between the knobs, the knobs never cross, and `minimumDistance` keeps a gap between them.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSRangeSlider.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSRangeSlider.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup. Copying sources instead? `DSRangeSlider` shares its value mapping with [DSSlider](DSSlider.md), so `velvet.swift add DSRangeSlider` copies both.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct PriceFilterDemo: View {
    @State private var price: ClosedRange<Double> = 100...400

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                HStack {
                    Text("Price").ds(.title3)
                    Spacer()
                    Text("$\(Int(price.lowerBound)) – $\(Int(price.upperBound))").ds(.numeric)
                }
                DSRangeSlider(range: $price, in: 0...500, step: 25, minimumDistance: 50)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Price")
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

The slider draws no values of its own. Show a read-out beside it, as above.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `range` | `Binding<ClosedRange<Double>>` | required | The selected span. It is kept inside `in`, on the notches and at least `minimumDistance` wide; a range that breaks those rules is corrected and written back. |
| `bounds` | `ClosedRange<Double>` | `0...1` | Allowed values. Declared as `in bounds:` at the call site. Both ends must be finite. |
| `step` | `Double?` | `nil` | Snap increment, counted from the lower bound. `nil`, zero or negative means continuous. The upper bound is always reachable, as in [DSSlider](DSSlider.md). |
| `minimumDistance` | `Double` | `0` | The smallest allowed `upperBound − lowerBound`. `0` lets the knobs meet. Negative or non-finite means `0`; it is capped at the width of `bounds`. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill between the knobs. Defaults to the theme accent. |

Correcting an invalid range: both ends are clamped into `bounds` and snapped to the nearest notch. If the range is then narrower than `minimumDistance`, the upper end moves up to the first notch that is far enough; when there is no room above, the range is pinned to the top of the track (`480...500` with a gap of 50 becomes `450...500`).

## Variants

```swift
struct RangeSliderVariantsDemo: View {
    @State private var hours: ClosedRange<Double> = 9...17
    @State private var level: ClosedRange<Double> = 0.2...0.7

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
            // Whole hours, at least two of them.
            DSRangeSlider(range: $hours, in: 0...24, step: 1, minimumDistance: 2)
            // Continuous 0...1, your own accent; the knobs may meet.
            DSRangeSlider(range: $level, accent: DSColors.secondary)
            // Dimmed and inert.
            DSRangeSlider(range: $level).disabled(true)
        }
    }
}
```

## Behavior

- Touching down grabs the nearer knob, which keeps following the finger until you lift it, so the knobs never swap mid-drag. A tap on the track moves the nearer knob there.
- When the knobs sit on top of each other, the side you drag toward decides which one moves. At the top of the track it is always the lower knob, since the upper one can't go further.
- A moving knob stops at the end of the track and at `minimumDistance` from the other knob. The other knob never moves.
- Haptics, as in [DSSlider](DSSlider.md): a stepped slider ticks (`.selection`) on each new notch; every slider fires one firm `.rigid` detent when the moving knob arrives at its limit, whether that is the end of the track or the gap. Grabbing a knob is silent.
- While grabbed, the knob lifts to 112% and a soft accent halo appears; it is drawn above the other knob.
- Reduce Motion: the knob doesn't lift and follows the finger with no spring lag; the halo stays, since it only changes opacity.
- Disabled (`.disabled(true)`): dimmed to 50% and ignores touches and VoiceOver adjustments.
- Reduce Transparency: nothing changes. The track is a flat fill, and the knobs are opaque.
- On a `dsBackdrop()` screen the track is the frosted wash; on a plain screen it is the neutral grey DSSlider uses.

## Accessibility

- Two adjustable elements, "Minimum" and "Maximum", inside a container. Put your own label on the container with `.accessibilityLabel("Price")`; VoiceOver reads it as you enter the slider.
- Swipe up or down on a knob to move it one notch (a tenth of the range for a continuous slider). It stops where a drag would, and each move fires a selection tick.
- Values read like DSSlider's: "25 percent" for the default continuous `0...1`, otherwise the number itself ("100", "-2.5") with as many decimals as `step` needs.
- Dynamic Type: nothing in the control scales; the 44 pt hit area is fixed.

## See also

- [DSSlider](DSSlider.md)
- [DSStepper](DSStepper.md)
- [DSChip](DSChip.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSLikeButton.md -->

# DSLikeButton

A favorite / like / bookmark toggle with a satisfying beat: the symbol swaps to its filled variant with a designed SF Symbols transition, springs up in a quick pop, and a single soft halo radiates out and fades. An optional count rolls when it changes. Turning it off is quiet.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSLikeButton.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSLikeButton.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct LikeDemo: View {
    @State private var isLiked = false
    @State private var likes = 128

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            DSLikeButton(isLiked: $isLiked, count: likes, accessibilityLabel: "Like post")
                .onChange(of: isLiked) { _, liked in
                    likes += liked ? 1 : -1
                }
                .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isLiked` | `Binding<Bool>` | required | The liked state. Tapping toggles it. |
| `count` | `Int?` | `nil` | A value shown beside the symbol; rolls with `.numericText` when it changes. `nil` hides it. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xl` (24) | Point size of the symbol. The tap target is at least 44 pt whatever the size. |
| `symbol` | `String` | `"heart.fill"` | The filled symbol shown while liked. |
| `emptySymbol` | `String` | `"heart"` | The outline symbol shown while not liked. |
| `tint` | `Color?` | `nil` | Color while liked, and of the halo. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.soft` | Fired on every tap, on the peak of the pop when liking. |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `String` | `"Like"` | What VoiceOver reads for the control. Pass one that matches the symbol (`"Favorite"`, `"Save"`). |

## Variants

```swift
HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.xl) {
    DSLikeButton(isLiked: .constant(true))                              // heart
    DSLikeButton(isLiked: .constant(true), symbol: "star.fill",
                 emptySymbol: "star", tint: DSColors.warning,
                 accessibilityLabel: "Favorite")                        // star
    DSLikeButton(isLiked: .constant(false), symbol: "bookmark.fill",
                 emptySymbol: "bookmark", accessibilityLabel: "Save")   // bookmark
}
```

Any filled/outline SF Symbol pair works — the replace transition morphs between them.

## Behavior

- Tapping flips the binding. Liking (off → on) plays the beat: the symbol swaps with `contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace))`, the glyph pops to 1.28× and springs back, and one filled halo in the tint radiates out and fades. The symbol and color ride a `DSAnimation.springSnappy`; the pop and halo run on a `keyframeAnimator` track, the same split as `DSSuccessCheck`.
- The haptic (`.soft` by default) fires on the peak of the pop, 0.13 s after the tap, so the buzz and the visual climax land together.
- Unliking (on → off) is quiet: the symbol swaps back and the color fades, with no pop and no halo. The haptic fires on the tap, since there is no beat to wait for. Unliking while a quick like is still popping ends the pop on the spot.
- Rapid taps never stack. Each like restarts the one keyframe track (and replaces the pending haptic), so there is never more than one pop or one halo on screen.
- The beat belongs to the tap. Setting `isLiked` from code (restoring saved state when a feed loads, a double-tap on a photo) swaps the symbol quietly, with no pop and no haptic.
- A `count` rolls with `.numericText` whenever it changes; drive it from the same state with `.onChange`.
- The tap target is at least 44 × 44 pt, whatever the `size`, and the button dips with `DSPress.iconScale` while pressed. Disabled, it dims.
- Reduce Motion: no pop and no halo, and the symbol swap and the count crossfade instead of morphing and rolling. The symbol and color still change and the haptic still fires, on the tap.
- The halo extends past `size`, so leave a little room around the button.

## Accessibility

- Exposed as a toggle button with your `accessibilityLabel` and a value of "Liked" or "Not liked" (with the count appended when present, e.g. "Liked, 129"). The value updates when the state changes.
- The visible count is hidden from VoiceOver to avoid reading it twice; it is carried in the value instead.
- The tap target is at least 44 pt even when the symbol is small.

## See also

- [DSSuccessCheck](DSSuccessCheck.md) for a one-shot success seal with the same halo mechanism
- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md) for an on/off setting switch
- [DSRating](DSRating.md) for a multi-step star rating
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSKeypad.md -->

# DSKeypad

An on-screen numeric keypad for the screens where the system keyboard is the wrong tool: an amount to send or tip, a passcode, a quantity at a kiosk. Twelve keys on a 3 × 4 grid: 1–9, then the decimal separator (only for amounts), 0 and delete. Keys dip and tick under your finger; a key that would make the value invalid wiggles and buzzes instead of typing.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSKeypad.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSKeypad.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct SendMoneyDemo: View {
    @State private var amount = ""

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.xl) {
                Text(amount.isEmpty ? "$0" : "$" + amount)
                    .ds(.displayMedium)
                    .accessibilityLabel("Amount")
                DSKeypad(text: $amount, maxLength: 7, decimalPlaces: 2)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

The keypad edits a `String`, because what people type is text until they're done: `"12."` and `"0.50"` are valid amounts in progress that no `Double` can hold. Like [DSSlider](DSSlider.md), it draws no value of its own: show your own read-out above it (a currency amount, PIN dots), as above.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | `Binding<String>` | required | The entered text. Keys append to it and delete from its end. |
| `maxLength` | `Int?` | `nil` | The most digits it may hold; the separator doesn't count. `nil` (or less than 1) means no limit. Use `4` or `6` for a PIN. |
| `decimalPlaces` | `Int` | `0` | Digits allowed after the decimal separator. `0` hides the separator key and keeps leading zeros (a PIN, a code, a count). Use `2` for money. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.light` | Fired on every accepted key. A refused key always fires `.warning`. |

### The rules

- **Digits** append, up to `maxLength` digits.
- **Amounts** (`decimalPlaces > 0`) never read `"05"` or `"00"`: a lone leading `0` is replaced by the next digit, and a second `0` is refused. Zeros after the separator are kept (`"0.05"`).
- **The separator** is accepted once. Typed first, it becomes `"0."`. After it, at most `decimalPlaces` digits fit.
- **Delete** removes the last character (the separator included) and is refused on empty text.
- **PINs and codes** (`decimalPlaces: 0`) keep every digit as typed, leading zeros included (`"007"`).

## Variants

```swift
struct PasscodeDemo: View {
    @State private var pin = ""
    @DSThemed private var theme

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.xl) {
            HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                ForEach(0..<4, id: \.self) { index in
                    Circle()
                        .fill(index < pin.count ? theme.accent : theme.subtleFill)
                        .frame(width: DSSpacing.sm, height: DSSpacing.sm)
                }
            }
            .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore)
            .accessibilityLabel("Passcode")
            .accessibilityValue("\(pin.count) of 4 digits")
            DSKeypad(text: $pin, maxLength: 4)
                .onChange(of: pin) { _, code in
                    if code.count == 4 { /* verify the code, then clear it */ }
                }
        }
    }
}
```

## Behavior

- Every key dips to `DSPress.scale` on a spring while held, and a faint ink wash deepens it.
- Digit keys sit on `theme.subtleFill` (the frosted wash on a backdrop, a flat nested fill on a card), never glass on glass. The separator and delete keys are bare glyphs, so the digits read as the keyboard.
- An accepted key fires `haptic` (a light tap by default). A refused key leaves the text alone, fires `.warning` and wiggles that key once with `dsJiggle`, the same refusal [DSStepper](DSStepper.md) gives at its bounds.
- **Locale.** The separator follows the `\.locale` environment: `"."` in en_US, `","` in de_DE. The bound text uses that separator, so parse it with the same locale, e.g. `Decimal(string: text, locale: locale)`.
- **Reduce Motion:** the refusal wiggle rests (it's a `DSMotion` effect); the warning haptic still says no. The press dip stays, since it follows your finger.
- **Disabled** (`.disabled(true)`): dimmed to 50%, and the keys ignore touches.
- Keys are 64 pt tall and share the width equally, so they stay well above the 44 pt minimum on every iPhone.

## Accessibility

- The pad is a container labelled "Keypad". Each key is its own button with the keyboard-key trait, read as its digit, "Decimal point" or "Delete", so VoiceOver's typing modes work on it.
- The keypad has no value of its own: give your read-out a label and value (`.accessibilityLabel("Amount")`, or `"Passcode"` with `"2 of 4 digits"` for PIN dots, as above), so people hear what they've typed. Don't speak a PIN's digits.
- Dynamic Type: the key glyphs scale with `.ds(.title1)` / `.dsFont(.title2)`; the 64 pt key height is a minimum, so larger text grows the keys.

## See also

- [DSCodeField](DSCodeField.md): one-time codes with SMS autofill, on the system keyboard.
- [DSStepper](DSStepper.md)
- [DSSlider](DSSlider.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

---
<!-- source: docs/components/DSTiltCard.md -->

# DSTiltCard

A glass card that tips in 3D toward your finger as you drag, with a specular highlight that slides across the surface like light on glass, then springs back to rest on release.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSTiltCard.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSTiltCard.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct TiltDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack {
                DSTiltCard {
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                        Image(systemName: "creditcard.fill").font(.title2)
                        Text("Velvet Card").ds(.title2)
                        Text("•••• •••• •••• 2048").ds(.numeric)
                    }
                    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

`DSTiltCard(maxTilt:padding:cornerRadius:haptic:content:)`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxTilt` | `Angle?` | `nil` | Peak rotation reached at the edge of the drag. `nil` is 12°. |
| `padding` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.md` | Inner padding around the content. |
| `cornerRadius` | `CGFloat` | `DSRadius.card` | Corner radius of the glass surface. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `.soft` | Fired once when the touch begins. `nil` for none. |
| `content` | `() -> Content` | required | The card's content (trailing closure). |

## Variants

```swift
VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
    // A wider tilt, no haptic
    DSTiltCard(maxTilt: .degrees(20), haptic: nil) {
        Text("Weekly streak").ds(.title3)
            .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
    }

    // Tighter corners, buttons inside keep working
    DSTiltCard(padding: DSSpacing.lg, cornerRadius: DSRadius.surface) {
        DSButton("Redeem", isFullWidth: true) {}
    }
}
```

## Behavior

- Dragging tips the card in 3D: horizontal drag rotates it around the vertical axis, vertical drag around the horizontal one, so the surface leans toward the finger. The tilt clamps at `maxTilt` once the drag passes ~120 pt from where it started.
- A specular sheen fades in with the tilt and slides across the glass, reading as light catching the glass rather than as a fill. It sits between the glass and the content, so text and icons keep full contrast. It rides the same white highlight language as `DSWash.edge` and `dsEdgeSweep`, a little stronger on light themes.
- The shadow deepens from `.lg` to `.xl` while the card is held.
- Release (or a cancelled touch) springs the card flat with `DSAnimation.springGentle`. While the finger is down the tilt follows it 1:1 with no animation, so it never lags.
- A `.soft` haptic fires once when the touch begins.
- The gesture is simultaneous: a card inside a `ScrollView` does not block scrolling (if the scroll takes over the touch, the card springs flat), and controls inside the card keep their taps.
- macOS: it follows a mouse drag in the same way. There is no haptic.

## Accessibility

- One container element (`.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)`): the content's own elements are read as they are, since the tilt is purely visual.
- **Reduce Motion:** the card never rotates, the shadow does not lift and the sheen does not slide. It rests as an ordinary glass surface and, while held, a still sheen fades in, so a touch still gets visible feedback without movement. The haptic still fires.
- **Reduce Transparency:** the glass surface falls back to a solid fill via `dsSurface`.
- Dynamic Type: all text uses `.ds(_:)` and scales with the user's text size.

## See also

- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [DSInteractiveCard](DSCard.md)
- [Motion primitives](Motion.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSDisclosureGroup.md -->

# DSDisclosureGroup

A glass "show more" section. Tap the header and the body springs open while the chevron rotates and a light haptic fires — the Velvet reading of an accordion / FAQ row, for settings detail, filters, long descriptions, anything that should stay out of the way until asked for.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSDisclosureGroup.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSDisclosureGroup.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(gradient: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct FAQDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                DSDisclosureGroup("Can I cancel anytime?") {
                    Text("Yes — cancel from Settings and keep access until the end of the period.")
                        .ds(.callout, color: DSColors.textSecondary)
                }
                DSDisclosureGroup("What's included", subtitle: "3 items", icon: "shippingbox") {
                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                        Text("• Unlimited projects").ds(.callout)
                        Text("• Priority support").ds(.callout)
                        Text("• Early access to betas").ds(.callout)
                    }
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `String` | required | The header label, always visible. Passed as the first, unlabeled argument. |
| `subtitle` | `String?` | `nil` | Optional secondary line under the title. |
| `icon` | `String?` | `nil` | Optional SF Symbol before the title, tinted with `theme.accent`. |
| `initiallyExpanded` | `Bool` | `false` | Open state on first appearance (self-contained init only). |
| `isExpanded` | `Binding<Bool>` | — | Drive the open state yourself (bound init). Use it for an "only one open at a time" accordion. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.light` | Feedback fired on each toggle. |
| `content` | `() -> Content` | required | The body revealed when expanded. |

There are two initializers: one that tracks its own state (`initiallyExpanded:`) and one you drive with a `Binding` (`isExpanded:`). Everything else is shared.

## Variants

```swift
// Self-contained, starts open, softer haptic
DSDisclosureGroup("Details", initiallyExpanded: true, haptic: .soft) {
    Text("Open on first appearance, with a softer tap.").ds(.callout)
}

// Controlled: one open at a time
@State private var open: Int? = 0

ForEach(0..<3, id: \.self) { index in
    DSDisclosureGroup("Section \(index + 1)", isExpanded: Binding(
        get: { open == index },
        set: { open = $0 ? index : nil }
    )) {
        Text("Only one section is open at a time.").ds(.callout)
    }
}
```

## Behavior

- Toggling springs the body open and closed with `DSAnimation.springSmooth`. The card grows with the body instead of the body popping in, the body fades with it, and the chevron rotates 180° on the same spring.
- The body is always laid out at its full height and clipped to the revealed part, so text never re-wraps or jumps while it opens.
- The motion is driven by the open state itself, so it also plays when you flip a bound `isExpanded` from outside (a toggle, a "collapse all" button) and when taps arrive in quick succession: the spring retargets instead of restarting.
- A `.light` haptic fires on every toggle (configurable via `haptic:`).
- A hairline `theme.palette.divider` separates the header from the body when open.
- The header dips with `DSPress.scale` while pressed.
- The body stays in the view tree while collapsed, so it keeps its `@State`. It is hidden from touch and VoiceOver, but it is still built: keep it light, or gate expensive content on your own state.
- Reduce Motion: the spring is replaced by a short ease (`DSAnimation.fast`), so the body reaches the same state without bounce. The haptic still fires.
- Reduce Transparency: the glass surface becomes a solid elevated background.

## Accessibility

- The header is one combined button element: VoiceOver reads the title (and subtitle), the trait "Button", and the value "Expanded" or "Collapsed". It updates when the state changes.
- The hint says what activating the header does: "Shows the details" or "Hides the details".
- The leading icon and the chevron are decorative and hidden from VoiceOver.
- While collapsed, the body is hidden from VoiceOver and cannot be tapped.
- Dynamic Type: the title uses `.ds(.title3)` and the subtitle `.ds(.footnote)`, the icon and chevron scale with them; body text scales with whatever `.ds(_:)` style you pass.

## See also

- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [DSListCell](DSListCell.md)
- [DSSheet](DSSheet.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)
