<!-- source: docs/components/DSTimeline.md -->

# DSTimeline

A vertical progress timeline: a rail of nodes joined by a connector that fills as the flow advances. The classic order-status pattern — Ordered → Shipped → Out for delivery → Delivered — and equally at home in multi-step flows, activity histories and wizards. It is the vertical, content-bearing complement to [`DSStepProgress`](Progress.md) (a row of flat capsules with no labels).

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSTimeline.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSTimeline.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct TimelineDemo: View {
    @State private var step = 2

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            DSCard {
                DSTimeline(
                    [
                        DSTimelineItem("Order placed", subtitle: "March 3, 9:41 AM", icon: "bag"),
                        DSTimelineItem("Shipped", subtitle: "Picked up by courier", icon: "shippingbox"),
                        DSTimelineItem("Out for delivery", subtitle: "Arriving today", icon: "box.truck"),
                        DSTimelineItem("Delivered", icon: "house")
                    ],
                    currentStep: step
                )
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `[DSTimelineItem]` | required | The stops, top to bottom. |
| `currentStep` | `Int` | required | Index of the live step. Steps before it are complete, the one at it is current, steps after it are upcoming. Pass `items.count` when every step is done. |
| `nodeSize` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxl` (32) | Diameter of each node at the default text size. It scales with Dynamic Type; the glyph and glow follow it. |
| `lineWidth` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxxs` (2) | Thickness of the connector rail. |
| `accent` | `Color?` | `nil` | Fill for reached nodes and the filled connector. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `haptics` | `Bool` | `true` | Fire a `.success` tick when the flow advances. |

`DSTimelineItem(_ title:, subtitle:, icon:)` — `subtitle` and `icon` (an SF Symbol) are optional.

## States

Each step derives its look from `currentStep`:

| Step | Node | Label | Connector below |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before `currentStep` | Accent fill, checkmark (or the item's icon) | `textPrimary` | Accent, filled |
| At `currentStep` | Accent fill, icon or dot, a glow that breathes | `textPrimary` | Empty |
| After `currentStep` | Muted fill, muted icon or empty | `textTertiary` | Empty |

`currentStep` is clamped to `0...items.count`. Pass `items.count` for "everything is done".

## Behavior

- Advancing `currentStep` grows the connector fill from the top and recolors the node with `DSAnimation.springSmooth`. The fill is clipped to its track, so the spring's overshoot never bleeds into the next node.
- The animation and the haptic are keyed on the step, not on appearance. A timeline that opens already at step 3 shows step 3 at once, with no fill and no haptic; only a forward change plays them.
- A `.success` haptic fires once when `currentStep` moves forward, however many steps it jumps (set `haptics: false` to silence it). None on first appearance, when moving back, or when a request past the end is clamped to where it already was.
- The live node carries a `.glow` that breathes (`dsBreathe(.medium)`) on its own layer behind the node, so the node itself never cross-fades when the step changes.
- Rows enter with the shared `dsStaggerIn` cascade.
- The title line is at least a node tall and centred in that height, so each node sits on its title at every text size. Long titles and subtitles wrap and the node stays on the first line.
- The timeline takes its height from its rows. It does not stretch to fill a taller container.
- No borders: nodes are filled circles, the connector is a capsule fill over a track in the palette border tone.
- Reduce Motion: the fill does not grow, it fades in; the live glow rests still; rows appear without the cascade.

## Accessibility

- Each step is one element. VoiceOver reads the title and subtitle as the label and the status ("Completed", "In progress", "Upcoming") as the value.
- Nodes, glyphs and connectors are hidden from VoiceOver; the status is carried by the value, not by color alone.
- Labels and nodes scale with Dynamic Type through the DS text styles and a scaled node size.

## See also

- [DSStepProgress](Progress.md)
- [DSSuccessCheck](DSSuccessCheck.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSExpandableText.md -->

# DSExpandableText

A block of copy that collapses to a few lines and springs open on tap, with a rotating chevron and a crossfading **Show more** / **Show less** affordance. For product descriptions, reviews, bios and terms — anywhere a long paragraph would otherwise push everything else off the screen or get truncated with no way back.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSExpandableText.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSExpandableText.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ExpandableTextDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            DSCard {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                    Text("About").ds(.title3)
                    DSExpandableText(
                        "Velvet UI is a small, opinionated SwiftUI library: frosted glass over a calm page tone, spring motion on everything you touch, and haptics that make the interface feel alive.",
                        lineLimit: 3
                    )
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

The toggle appears only when the copy is actually clipped: pass short text and `DSExpandableText` renders it with no affordance.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_ text` | `String` | required | The copy to show. Read in full by VoiceOver even while clipped. |
| `lineLimit` | `Int` | `3` | Lines shown while collapsed. |
| `expandLabel` | `String` | `"Show more"` | The reveal affordance. |
| `collapseLabel` | `String` | `"Show less"` | The collapse affordance. |
| `style` | `DSTextStyle` | `.body` | Text style for the copy. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Copy color. `nil` follows the theme (`textPrimary`). |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.light` | Feedback fired on toggle. |

## Variants

```swift
struct ExpandableTextVariantsDemo: View {
    @DSThemed private var theme
    let longCopy: String

    var body: some View {
        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
            // Two lines, custom labels
            DSExpandableText(
                longCopy,
                lineLimit: 2,
                expandLabel: "Read more",
                collapseLabel: "Read less"
            )

            // Secondary copy
            DSExpandableText(longCopy, style: .callout, color: theme.palette.textSecondary)

            // Fits on two lines, so no toggle appears
            DSExpandableText("Short copy needs no toggle.")
        }
    }
}
```

## Behavior

- Truncation is measured, not guessed: two off-screen copies of the text (one clamped to `lineLimit`, one unbounded) are laid out at the real text width with `onGeometryChange`, and the toggle shows only when the unbounded copy is taller. Short copy renders with no toggle at all. Neither copy depends on the expanded state, so the toggle never flickers mid-reveal, and it appears or disappears by itself when the text, the line limit, the width or the text size changes.
- The reveal animates a clipped frame, not the line limit. The full paragraph is laid out once and the frame (pinned to the top) grows from `lineLimit` lines to the full height with `DSAnimation.springSmooth`, so lines are uncovered in place: nothing re-wraps, re-centres or jumps while it moves. The ellipsis on the last collapsed line is swapped only while it is hidden behind the clip: at the start of an expand and once the collapse has settled.
- The chevron rotates 180° and the label crossfades with `.contentTransition(.opacity)` on the same spring.
- The configurable haptic (`.light` by default) fires on each toggle, on the tap.
- `lineLimit` below 1 means 1.
- Reduce Motion: the reveal is instant (no spring, no rotation sweep); the text and toggle still work.
- The text style applied through `.ds(_:)` scales with Dynamic Type, and the measurement re-runs at the new size.

## Accessibility

- The copy is a standard `Text`, so VoiceOver reads it in full whether collapsed or expanded, even while the last lines are clipped.
- The toggle is a button labelled with its visible text ("Show more" / "Show less", so Voice Control can say it) with the value "Collapsed" or "Expanded". The chevron is hidden from VoiceOver, and the measuring copies never appear to it.
- The toggle row has padding above and below the label to make a larger tap target than the text line.

## See also

- [DSTypewriterText](DSTypewriterText.md)
- [DSCard](DSCard.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSCheckbox.md -->

# DSCheckbox

A themed checkbox for lists, forms and consent rows: an empty ring-shaped box that pops to the accent while its checkmark draws on, with a rigid haptic.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSCheckbox.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSCheckbox.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct CheckboxDemo: View {
    @State private var acceptsTerms = true
    @State private var newsletter = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            DSCard {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xxs) {
                    DSCheckbox("I accept the terms and conditions", isOn: $acceptsTerms)
                    DSCheckbox("Send me the newsletter", isOn: $newsletter)
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | `String?` | `nil` | Text beside the box (unlabeled first argument). The label is part of the tap target. |
| `isOn` | `Binding<Bool>` | required | The checked state. |
| `size` | `DSCheckboxSize` | `.medium` | `.small` (20 pt box), `.medium` (24 pt) or `.large` (28 pt). |
| `onColor` | `Color?` | `nil` | Box fill while checked. Defaults to the theme accent. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle` | `.rigid` | Haptic fired on every change. |

## Variants

```swift
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xxs) {
    DSCheckbox("Compact row", isOn: $compact, size: .small)
    DSCheckbox("Order confirmed", isOn: $confirmed, onColor: theme.palette.success)
    DSCheckbox(isOn: $selectAll, size: .large)
        .accessibilityLabel("Select all")
}
```
Here `theme` is `@DSThemed private var theme`. Without a label it is just the box, for use in your own rows; give it a VoiceOver label yourself.

## Behavior

- Tapping the box **or its label** toggles `isOn`, fires the haptic and plays the animation. A disabled checkbox dims to 50 % and ignores taps.
- The box always lays out at least 44×44 pt, so the hit target meets Apple's minimum at every size. `.small` shrinks the box, not the row; in a dense list, drop the stack spacing to zero.
- Checking: the accent layer springs up from 55 % size with `DSAnimation.springBouncy` and fades in, and the checkmark draws on (`trim`) a beat later. Unchecking: the tick undraws at once while the layer shrinks and fades.
- The animation follows `isOn`, so it also plays when the binding changes from outside (a "select all" parent). A checkbox that appears already checked, for example one scrolling into a lazy list, shows the finished tick without replaying the draw.
- The unchecked box is a filled ring: an outer shape in `palette.textSecondary` (at least 3:1 against the card in light and dark, WCAG 1.4.11) and an inner one in `palette.backgroundElevated`, plus the specular `dsWashEdge`. Both are fills; there is no stroke.
- The tick is `theme.onAccent` on the accent fill, and `palette.textOnPrimary` when you pass your own `onColor`.
- Reduce Motion: nothing pops or draws. The box crossfades, and the tick is simply there when checked.
- Press: the row dips with `DSPress` (the lone box dips with `DSPress.iconScale`).

## Accessibility

- One element. Its label is the `label` text; add `.accessibilityLabel("…")` when you use the box without one.
- Value is "Checked" or "Unchecked". It carries the toggle trait, plus the selected trait while checked, and reads as dimmed when `.disabled`.
- Dynamic Type: the label text scales with the user's text size. The box and the 44 pt minimum stay fixed.

## See also

- [DSToggle](DSToggle.md)
- [DSSegmentedControl](DSSegmentedControl.md)
- [DSListCell](DSListCell.md)
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSFlipCard.md -->

# DSFlipCard

A two-sided glass card that turns over in 3D to reveal its back — tap it, or drive it from a binding. The flip is a single spring about one axis with a touch of perspective, and it fires a haptic on the turn.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSFlipCard.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSFlipCard.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct FlipDemo: View {
    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            // Tap anywhere on the card to turn it over.
            DSFlipCard {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                    Text("This month").ds(.footnote)
                    Text("1 248").ds(.displayMedium)
                    Text("Tap to see the trend").ds(.callout)
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            } back: {
                VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xs) {
                    Text("vs. last month").ds(.footnote)
                    Text("+12%").ds(.displayMedium)
                    Text("Tap to flip back").ds(.callout)
                }
                .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

Glass looks best over `.dsBackdrop()` or `DSScreen(backdrop: true)`. The card takes the size of the larger face and both faces fill it, so the card keeps its frame when it turns. Give the card a fixed `.frame(...)` to size it yourself.

### Drive it from a binding

Pass `isFlipped` to turn the card over from code (a button, a gesture, a result) as well as by tapping. The card animates the turn itself whenever `isFlipped` changes, so no `withAnimation` is needed.

```swift
struct CardFace: View {
    @State private var revealed = false

    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
            DSFlipCard(isFlipped: $revealed, axis: .vertical) {
                Text("•••• 4242").ds(.numeric)
            } back: {
                Text("CVC 123 · 09/28").ds(.numeric)
            }

            DSButton(revealed ? "Hide" : "Reveal", variant: .secondary, size: .small) {
                withAnimation(DSAnimation.springSmooth) { revealed.toggle() }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

When a face holds its own controls, set `flipOnTap: false` so taps reach them and the card flips only from the binding.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isFlipped` | `Binding<Bool>` | — | Only on the bound initializer: `false` shows `front`, `true` shows `back`. Omit it for a self-managing, tap-to-flip card. |
| `axis` | `DSFlipAxis` | `.horizontal` | Which way the card swings: `.horizontal` (left-to-right) or `.vertical` (top-to-bottom). |
| `style` | `DSCardStyle` | `.elevated` | Glass treatment of each face, same as `DSCard`: `.flat`, `.elevated`, `.outlined`. |
| `padding` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.md` | Inner padding of each face. |
| `cornerRadius` | `CGFloat` | `DSRadius.card` | Corner radius of each face (20). |
| `flipOnTap` | `Bool` | `true` | Turn the card over when it is tapped. Set `false` when a face has its own controls. |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `.rigid` | Haptic fired on every turn, tap or binding. `nil` for none. |
| `front` | `@ViewBuilder () -> Front` | required | The face shown at rest. |
| `back` | `@ViewBuilder () -> Back` | required | The face revealed after the turn. |

## Behavior

- The turn is one `DSAnimation.springSmooth` about `axis`, with a subtle perspective so the card reads as lifting off the glass.
- A single animated angle drives the turn through an `Animatable` container, so the two faces swap exactly at the 90° edge — no ghosting and no mirrored text. The back face is pre-rotated a half turn so it reads the right way round once flipped.
- Each face draws the same surfaces as `DSCard` (glass, the 1pt edge highlight, the soft shadow). While the card is turning, a solid body with its own shadow replaces the glass, which does not render while the 3D transform animates; the glass fades back in just under a second after the last flip. Under Reduce Transparency the glass becomes a solid elevated background.
- The turn fires `haptic` (default `.rigid`) as it starts, on both tap and programmatic flips (it follows `isFlipped`). Pass `nil` when your own control already fires one.
- A face that is not showing never takes touches, so controls on the front and back can share a position.
- **Reduce Motion:** the card does not turn; the faces crossfade with `DSAnimation.fast`.

## Accessibility

- With `flipOnTap` on, the card is one VoiceOver element with the `.isButton` trait, the hint "Double tap to flip" and the value "Front side" / "Back side" (announced on every turn); the visible face's content is read as the label.
- The hidden face is marked `.accessibilityHidden`, so VoiceOver never reads both sides at once.
- With `flipOnTap: false`, no button semantics are added and each face keeps its own hit testing and VoiceOver — label the flip control yourself.
- Text uses `.ds(_:)` styles, which scale with Dynamic Type; give both faces room to grow.

## See also

- [DSCard](DSCard.md) for the glass surface each face is built on
- [DSSuccessCheck](DSSuccessCheck.md) and [DSConfetti](DSConfetti.md) for other reveal moments
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSAvatarGroup.md -->

# DSAvatarGroup

A facepile: overlapping avatars that show who is on a thread, in a space or going to an event, with a "+N" bubble when there are more than fit.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSAvatarGroup.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSAvatarGroup.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct EventRow: View {
    @State private var showsGuests = false

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            DSCard {
                HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.md) {
                    DSAvatarGroup(
                        names: ["Ana Ruiz", "Ben Cole", "Cy Park", "Di Sol", "Eli Wu"],
                        maxVisible: 3
                    ) { showsGuests = true }

                    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.xxs) {
                        Text("Design Review").ds(.title3)
                        Text("5 people going").ds(.callout)
                    }
                    Spacer(minLength: 0)
                }
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
        .dsSheet(isPresented: $showsGuests) {
            Text("Guest list").ds(.title2).padding(DSSpacing.xl)
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

`DSAvatarGroup(members:maxVisible:size:overlap:haptic:action:)` and `DSAvatarGroup(names:…)`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `members` / `names` | `[DSAvatarGroup.Member]` / `[String]` | required | The people, first on top. `names` makes initials-only avatars. |
| `maxVisible` | `Int` | `4` | Most circles to show, the "+N" bubble included. At least 2. |
| `size` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxxl` | Diameter of each avatar. |
| `overlap` | `CGFloat` | `0.25` | How much each avatar is covered by the next, as a fraction of its width (`0...0.9`). |
| `haptic` | `DSHapticStyle?` | `.light` | Fired when the group is tapped (with `action`). `nil` for none. |
| `action` | `(() -> Void)?` | `nil` | Makes the whole group a button. |

`DSAvatarGroup.Member(id:name:imageURL:)`: `id` defaults to `name` and must be unique within the group; `imageURL` loads a photo with an initials fallback, like [DSAvatar](DSAvatar.md).

## Variants

```swift
VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
    // Photos where you have them, initials where you don't
    DSAvatarGroup(members: [
        .init(name: "Ada Lovelace", imageURL: URL(string: "https://picsum.photos/seed/ada/96")),
        .init(name: "Grace Hopper")
    ])

    // Small and tight
    DSAvatarGroup(names: ["Ana Ruiz", "Ben Cole", "Cy Park"], size: DSSpacing.xxl, overlap: 0.3)
}
```

## Behavior

- Built from `DSAvatar`, so it themes and scales with it.
- With more people than `maxVisible`, the last slot becomes a "+N" bubble counting everyone not shown.
- The gap between neighbours is a cut-out of the avatar in front, not a ring: nothing is stroked and there is no background colour to match, so the group looks right on a card, a plain page or a photo.
- Avatars pop in one after another. Adding a person pops in only the new one.
- With `action`, the group dips on press and fires a light haptic, then calls `action`. Keep the group at 32 pt or more if it is tappable.
- Reduce Motion: avatars fade in, nothing scales.
- Right-to-left layouts mirror the pile.

## Accessibility

- The group is one VoiceOver element. It names the people shown and counts the rest: "Ana, Ben and 3 others". With no overflow it names everyone ("Ana, Ben and Cy"); with nobody it reads "No people".
- With `action` it also has the button trait.
- Individual avatars and the "+N" bubble are not separately focusable.

## See also

- [DSAvatar](DSAvatar.md) for a single avatar
- [DSBadge](DSBadge.md) for counts and status marks
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/components/DSAudioBars.md -->

# DSAudioBars

An equaliser for live audio: a row of capsule bars that ripple while sound is playing or being recorded, follow an optional live level, and ease down to a flat line when idle.

**Platforms:** iOS 18+ · macOS 15+  ·  **Source:** [`DSAudioBars.swift`](../../Sources/VelvetUI/Components/DSAudioBars.swift)

## Install

```swift
// Package.swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git", from: "0.2.0")
// target dependencies
.product(name: "VelvetUI", package: "velvet-ui")
```

In Xcode: File → Add Package Dependencies… → paste `https://github.com/MatiasPC/velvet-ui.git`. Inject the theme once at your app root (`@State private var theme = DSTheme(style: .sunset)` + `.dsTheme(theme)`); see [the README](../../README.md#install) for the full setup.

## Usage

```swift
import VelvetUI

struct ListeningDemo: View {
    @State private var isListening = true
    @State private var micLevel = 0.5   // feed this from your recorder's meter

    var body: some View {
        DSScreen(backdrop: true) {
            VStack(spacing: DSSpacing.lg) {
                DSCard {
                    HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.sm) {
                        DSAudioBars(isActive: isListening, level: micLevel, barCount: 7)
                        Text(isListening ? "Listening…" : "Paused").ds(.callout)
                        Spacer()
                    }
                }
                DSToggle("Listening", isOn: $isListening)
            }
            .dsScreenPadding()
        }
    }
}
```

## Parameters

`DSAudioBars(isActive:level:barCount:barWidth:spacing:height:color:)`

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `isActive` | `Bool` | `true` | Ripple while true; ease down to a flat line while false. |
| `level` | `Double?` | `nil` | Live level `0...1`, the amplitude of the ripple. `nil` ripples at full amplitude. Out-of-range values are clamped. |
| `barCount` | `Int` | `5` | Number of bars (at least 1). |
| `barWidth` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxs` | Width of each bar. |
| `spacing` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xxs` | Gap between bars. |
| `height` | `CGFloat` | `DSSpacing.xl` | Height of the tallest bar. |
| `color` | `Color?` | `nil` | Bar fill. Defaults to the theme accent. |

## Variants

```swift
HStack(spacing: DSSpacing.xl) {
    DSAudioBars(barCount: 3)
    DSAudioBars(barCount: 7, height: DSSpacing.xxl)
    DSAudioBars(barCount: 5, color: DSColors.success)
}
```
Few and short for a list row, many and tall for a voice screen.

## Behavior

- Heights come from one clock, with a phase offset per bar, so the row ripples rather than pulses.
- Going between active and idle, and between levels, eases with the system's eased curves (not a spring: nothing was touched). Raw meter readings are fine to pass; a level change is smoothed over about a quarter of a second.
- With a `level`, the bars swell with it and sit at the resting line at `0`. Without one they ripple at full amplitude.
- The clock is paused when the bars are idle, when the view is not on screen (it disappeared, for example behind a pushed screen), when the app is not active, and under Reduce Motion. A paused indicator costs no CPU. In a plain `ScrollView` a row that is only scrolled away may still count as on screen; lists and lazy stacks unload it.
- Reduce Motion: no ripple. Idle bars are a flat line; active bars rest on a symmetric bell, and `level` is ignored.

## Accessibility

- The bars are decorative and hidden from VoiceOver. Put a label next to them ("Listening…") so the state is also announced.

## See also

- [DSThinkingIndicator](DSThinkingIndicator.md) for "the assistant is working"
- [Motion](Motion.md) for ambient effects on any view
- [All components](../../README.md#components) · [Theming](../../README.md#theming)

<!-- source: docs/examples/Onboarding.md -->

# Onboarding

A four-page onboarding: welcome, theme picker, notification preferences and a celebratory finish.

> Example — not a component. Copy it and adapt it.

**Source:** [`OnboardingFlow.swift`](../../Examples/VelvetGallery/VelvetGallery/Flows/OnboardingFlow.swift)

## What it demonstrates

- [DSButton](../components/DSButton.md): one full-width button that reads "Continue", then "Get started" on the last page.
- [DSPageControl](../components/DSPageControl.md): dots that follow the swipe and jump on tap.
- [DSTypewriterText](../components/DSTypewriterText.md): the welcome headline cycling through short phrases.
- [DSCard](../components/DSCard.md), [DSToggle](../components/DSToggle.md) and [DSSegmentedControl](../components/DSSegmentedControl.md): the preferences page.
- [DSSuccessCheck](../components/DSSuccessCheck.md) and [DSConfetti](../components/DSConfetti.md): the finish.
- Motion modifiers: `.dsBreathe(.subtle)` on the glyph and `.dsPopIn(delay:)` for staggered entrances ([Motion](../components/Motion.md)).

## How it works

- The flow owns a `DSTheme` in `@State` and injects it with `.dsTheme(theme)` at its root. The theme page sets `theme.style` inside `withAnimation(DSAnimation.normal)`, so the backdrop crossfades.
- Pages are a paging `TabView` on iOS. On macOS the flow shows the current page only.
- Each page builds its content only while it is the current page, so the pop-in stagger replays every visit.
- Arriving on the last page flips `DSSuccessCheck(isComplete:)` and bumps the confetti trigger on the same beat. The confetti is attached to the full-screen container, because it draws inside the view it is attached to.
- `onFinish` runs when you press "Get started".

## Run it

Gallery → Examples → Onboarding.

## Copy it

```bash
swift velvet.swift add Onboarding --dest MyApp/VelvetUI
```

<!-- source: docs/examples/Settings.md -->

# Settings

A settings screen with a profile header, preference toggles, a theme detail screen and a slide-to-confirm account deletion.

> Example — not a component. Copy it and adapt it.

**Source:** [`SettingsFlow.swift`](../../Examples/VelvetGallery/VelvetGallery/Flows/SettingsFlow.swift)

## What it demonstrates

- [DSCard](../components/DSCard.md), [DSAvatar](../components/DSAvatar.md) and [DSBadge](../components/DSBadge.md): the profile header.
- [DSListCell](../components/DSListCell.md) with `DSDivider` and `DSSectionHeader`: grouped rows inside `DSCard(padding: 0)`.
- [DSToggle](../components/DSToggle.md) and [DSSegmentedControl](../components/DSSegmentedControl.md): preferences.
- [DSSheet](../components/DSSheet.md) and [DSSlideToConfirm](../components/DSSlideToConfirm.md): the delete-account confirmation, tinted with the error color.
- [DSToast](../components/DSToast.md), presented with `.dsToast`: "Saved" feedback.

## How it works

- `SettingsFlow` has no `NavigationStack` of its own, because nested stacks are unsupported. The host provides one (the Gallery pushes it inside its list's stack); wrap it in `NavigationStack { SettingsFlow() }` to show it standalone.
- Appearance (System, Light, Dark) really drives `.preferredColorScheme` on the flow.
- The Theme row pushes a detail screen. Choosing a theme sets `theme.style` in `withAnimation`, so the backdrop crossfades behind the navigation bar.
- Changing any toggle, the appearance or the theme shows a "Saved" toast for about 1.6 s. There is one toast at a time: `.dsToast` replaces the old one with the new and restarts the timer, and the user can flick it away.
- "Delete account" opens a sheet. The slide awaits a fake service, shows "Deleted", then the sheet closes and a toast confirms.
- Email and Password rows are navigation rows that show an info toast, to keep the example short.

## Run it

Gallery → Examples → Settings.

## Copy it

```bash
swift velvet.swift add Settings --dest MyApp/VelvetUI
```

<!-- source: docs/examples/Checkout.md -->

# Checkout

A cart with quantity steppers, a promo code, a rolling total and a slide to pay that ends in a confirmation.

> Example — not a component. Copy it and adapt it.

**Source:** [`CheckoutFlow.swift`](../../Examples/VelvetGallery/VelvetGallery/Flows/CheckoutFlow.swift)

## What it demonstrates

- [DSCard](../components/DSCard.md) and [DSStepper](../components/DSStepper.md): line items, each stepper labelled with the item name for VoiceOver.
- [DSTextField](../components/DSTextField.md) and [DSButton](../components/DSButton.md): the promo code with success and error states.
- [DSNumberTicker](../components/DSNumberTicker.md): the total rolls whenever a quantity or the promo changes.
- [DSSlideToConfirm](../components/DSSlideToConfirm.md): pay, with `finish: .morphAndVanish` handing off to the success state.
- [DSSuccessCheck](../components/DSSuccessCheck.md) and [DSConfetti](../components/DSConfetti.md): the confirmation.
- [DSEmptyState](../components/DSEmptyState.md): the empty cart.

## How it works

- Try the code `VELVET` for 10% off. Any other code shows the error state. Editing the code clears the result.
- The slide's `onConfirm` awaits `CheckoutService.charge` (about 1.2 s). Turn on "Simulate a declined card" to make it throw: the control re-opens and a message explains why. While the charge runs the cart steppers, promo field and decline toggle are disabled, so the charged total is the one shown.
- On success the slide plays its `.morphAndVanish` finish; about 0.9 s later (in a cancellable `Task`) the view swaps to the confirmation with `DSAnimation.springSmooth`, and the confetti trigger is bumped on the same beat. The confirmation's `DSSuccessCheck` passes `haptic: nil`, so the payment has a single success haptic (the slide's). The confetti is attached to the root container, which covers the screen.
- "Done" calls `onFinish()`, resets the cart, and remounts the slide with a new `.id` so it starts fresh.
- Set every quantity to 0 to see the empty state with "Restore cart". The pay control is hidden while the cart is empty.

## Run it

Gallery → Examples → Checkout.

## Copy it

```bash
swift velvet.swift add Checkout --dest MyApp/VelvetUI
```
